task_name: Aurelian Skin - Ecommerce skincare image system
client_brief:
Make eight skincare products look like one launch, not eight shoots

Our launch range needs to look as considered online as it does on the shelf. At the moment the eight bottles look as though they belong to different brands.

What we need back
- Skincare product-page module: 8 named exports. The photograph shows the product named on this module. The bottle label remains legible at the delivered size. The product benefit is visually subordinate to the product name.
- Skincare range launch key visual: 1 named export. The composition identifies Aurelian Skin. The cleared launch claim is reproduced without a stronger efficacy claim. The product range is the primary visual focus.
- Retailer launch carousel: 5 named exports. The opening page identifies the range. The closing page presents the approved shopping action. The product sequence has a clear narrative.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Clinical skincare and personal care, actives-led, direct to consumer plus specialty retail
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024 in Boston, Massachusetts. A two person founder team, sold for a year to a waiting list and through two dermatology practices before the retail season.
brand_identity.about: Aurelian Skin is a small clinical skincare line built on eight actives-led products at thirty four to sixty eight dollars. In March we open our own online store and enter a specialty chain's twelve doors, so everything a customer sees changes at once. The line is meant to read like a laboratory with good taste: cool, quiet, evidence first, generous with white space and free of decoration. Not a spa, not a discount aisle. Our customer reads the ingredient list before the copy, and the brand is built to reward that: honest claims, clear INCI, restraint in place of ritual.
brand_identity.audience: Women roughly twenty six to forty two, ingredient literate, who research formulations and trust plainness over promise. They shop web stores and specialty beauty floors and judge a product by its panel.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Prestige-mass at thirty four to sixty eight dollars per SKU. Above the mass aisle, below luxury conserve pricing. The middle is the position, and the look must not drift warm and cheap or dark and precious.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained type system for all launch collateral: a clean grotesque for names and body copy carrying the ingredient literacy, with a single quiet display cut for the wordmark. Strong typography and whitespace do the work, no decorative faces.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, factual, unhurried. States what a product does and does not claim. Reads like a well-run lab that respects the reader, never breathless and never coy.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo file was lost when the first designer's drive failed. All that survives is a handheld photograph of an outer carton showing the mark printed in one deep ink: a small-caps lockup set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule. Recovering that mark as usable artwork is part of this engagement. No other source brand files remain.
brand_identity.values: Ingredient honesty, precision in every detail from panel to package, and clinical restraint: at this band, quiet and exact is the brand, and overstatement or gloss would undercut the claim.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Corner and Cure - Spring dish launch photography
client_brief:
Spring dish photography and a reusable printed card set for Corner & Cure

The spring dishes are ready. The photographs and printed cards are not. We run Corner & Cure, a neighbourhood cafe, and need someone comfortable moving between food retouching and small-format print production.

The commission

 Spring dish counter card: 11 named exports. The hero photograph shows the named dish. The dish description is readable at printed size. The plate retains natural food texture. The restaurant identity is visible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent all-day cafe and counter service, lunch sandwiches and bowls, small plates and wine after four, serving a neighbourhood in food and hospitality.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Brooklyn, New York; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Corner and Cure is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Brooklyn, New York, and this commission covers phase 1: food image system and seasonal launch assets.
brand_identity.audience: Neighbourhood regulars aged 25 to 45 who come in twice a week, know the counter staff, and read the screens over the pass from across the room. Local, food-literate, loyal, and quick to distrust anything that reads as styled to death.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-market all-day cafe. Mains 16 to 24 dollars, wine by the glass 11 to 15. Sits comfortably above fast-casual counters and well below the tasting-menu rooms downtown.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a warm humanist serif with a little ink to it, set large so a dish name reads across the counter. Text and prices in a plain, open sans that stays legible at small sizes. The feel is elevated but comfortable, closer to a chalkboard than a wine list.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, never fussy. We talk about burnt butter, the good bread and scrubbed oak, and we let the food carry the sentence. Example line: 'Small plates and a glass of something, most nights until late.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The printed table dish cards exist only as the flat file our printer sent to press last spring, and she has since retired, so there is no working layout and no editable source. The photographed dishes and the till copy Danny writes are the only current materials, and both are considered final.
brand_identity.values: Real portions, honest cooking, and copy that is never reworded or cut, because the allergen line matters.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Cedarline and Vale - Ridgeway Lane listing image system
client_brief:
Bring a mixed-light property shoot together for Ridgeway Lane

Property: Ridgeway Lane
Source: twelve room photographs
Use: listing gallery, portal crops and tall lead-room placements

Deliverables
1. Ridgeway Lane listing brochure: 1 named export. The cover identifies the actual property. The room sequence explains the property layout. Every property claim agrees with the supplied listing facts. The contact page includes the approved agent details.
2. Property portal hero: 1 named export. The hero depicts Ridgeway Lane rather than a stock property. The architectural verticals look plausible.
3. Room announcement: 3 named exports. The featured room matches the named property. The enquiry action is visible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Boutique residential real estate brokerage specialising in architect-designed listings, residential property in Marin County.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2012, Marin County, California. Six agents led by the principal, working a small book of high-value listings.
brand_identity.about: Cedarline and Vale is a six-agent brokerage in Marin that takes on architect-designed and materially serious homes. We present listings the way the architecture asks to be seen: quietly, accurately, and next to whatever three other agents are showing. Our credibility rests on buyers and vendors trusting that the pictures are the house.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 40 to 60 with household incomes above 400 thousand who read light and material as proxies for build quality, and vendors of design-led homes. They view our listings alongside three competing agents and notice anything that looks retouched.
brand_identity.price_positioning: High-value residential, flagship listings from the low millions up. Positioned above volume agencies and apart from developer marketing, on restraint and accuracy rather than gloss.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headings that does not announce itself, paired with a neutral grotesque for specification and body. Generous leading, wide margins, one photograph doing the work on a page. Type should read as calm and built, never decorative.
brand_identity.voice: Cool, restrained and true. We describe what is there and let the room speak. No superlatives, no cosiness, nothing that sounds sold. Example line: 'Glass on three sides, the bay through the living room, the oaks off the kitchen.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no working design source for the office window cards. Only the flat file the printer sent to press last year survives, and she has retired, so any change means rebuilding from that file. The feature sheet and portal module are expected to be handed back as editable documents because prices move.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over flattery: cool, restrained and honest, and nothing that reads as retouched.

task_name: Verranza Coastal Retreats - Villa collection image system
client_brief:
Three villas, one collection: imagery, crops and the gate monogram

For Verranza Coastal Retreats, the challenge is consistency without making three different villas interchangeable. We need the stone, limewash and coastal light to sit comfortably together across direct bookings and agent materials. The supplied do-not-want references are important.

Please prepare
- Villa booking hero: 3 named exports. The named villa matches the photograph. The offer price agrees with the approved rate record. The booking action is readable.
- Villa comparison brochure: 1 named export. Villa identities are unambiguous. The comparison makes differences between the properties easy to scan. Rates preserve their stated season.

brand_identity.values: Honest representation of a real place, true water and true stone, and a family mark used quietly.

task_name: Halcyon Quarter - Mixed-use launch photography
client_brief:
Evening-led property campaign from an overcast shoot

Halcyon Quarter is a former ropeworks development. The audience is downsizers looking carefully at the place, not people buying a dramatic sky. Our capture day was overcast; the campaign needs a credible evening direction across very different placements.

Final handoff

 Halcyon Quarter launch hoarding: 1 named export. The development name is legible at the specified scale. The pictured building remains faithful to the supplied development image. The enquiry action is visible.

 Mixed-use launch poster: 1 named export. The residential and commercial offer is distinguishable. The developer identity is visible.

 Property portal campaign panel: 1 named export. The approved location appears correctly. The composition does not imply completed construction where the source is a proposal.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Off-plan residential development launch on a former rope works site, sold through a boutique brokerage with a partner lender, real estate and property.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Beckett Wharf, Providence, Rhode Island. Halcyon Quarter is fifty two apartments by the developer Kestrel and Vane, phase one releasing in seven weeks, sold by Harbor Crest Realty with Kestrel Home Lending as finance partner.
brand_identity.about: Halcyon Quarter is a fifty two apartment scheme by Kestrel and Vane on the old rope works site at Beckett Wharf. Phase one sells to professional downsizers leaving a family home nearby. What the scheme sells is the evening: warm rooms against a cool blue hour on the water, quiet and expensive rather than shiny, carried across the developer, the brokerage and the lender as one look.
brand_identity.audience: Professional downsizers aged 50 to 65 leaving a house they have owned for thirty years within twenty miles. Discerning, unhurried, distrustful of shiny marketing, and likely to count windows when they visit the site.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium off-plan residential, apartments from 780 thousand to 1.45 million dollars. Positioned as quiet and expensive, above bright price-led property marketing and apart from investor rental stock.
brand_identity.typography: A text serif with real hierarchy carrying headings and pricing, set plainly inside the copy, paired with a restrained sans for captions and specification. Quiet and expensive: generous margins, one photograph per canvas, no starbursts and no heavy price treatment.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, assured and understated. Brass not gold, the water cold and the rooms warm, nothing shiny. We state the address, the light and the offer without overselling. Example line: 'Fifty two apartments on the water at Beckett Wharf, releasing this autumn.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The Kestrel and Vane monogram exists only as sign paint, brushed by the sign writer onto the site hoarding board, with a single photograph of it and no artwork file. The lender's payment cards survive only as the flat file their printer ran last spring, with no working source held by anyone, and every figure has since changed.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about an off-plan scheme (nothing shown that the building does not have) and one restrained look shared across developer, brokerage and lender.

client_brief:
Help us prepare Ada's family photographs for the reunion

Hello,

Scope
1. Archival restoration master: 9 named exports. The sitter remains faithful to the source photograph. Documentary details are not invented. Damage removal does not erase facial texture.
2. Family archive share image: 9 named exports. The full intended picture area is retained. The tone remains appropriate to the photographic era.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

brand_identity.sector: A private family archive of one woman, Ada Hollis, restored and framed for a home wall and a keepsake folio, not sold to anyone.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Assembled in 2026 at the family house in Vermont, New England, by three siblings in their sixties acting on behalf of twenty two relatives.
brand_identity.about: The archive holds nine photographs of Ada Hollis, who died in April at ninety nine, spanning roughly 1912 to 1974. It exists so that twenty two people who come home at Thanksgiving can hang one wall of her and carry one folio each. The standard is a museum label, not a memory book: honest, quiet, and true to what is actually in the photograph.
brand_identity.audience: Three siblings commissioning on behalf of twenty two family members aged 8 to 74. Not a commercial audience: the work hangs in a family house and is judged by people who knew Ada.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A private heritage commission of 650 to 1,600 dollars. The money buys restraint rather than effect: a true archival neutral, deep honest blacks, one photograph per page, generous margins, and visible respect for the grain and the paper each print is made of.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet text serif set the way a museum sets a wall label: small, calm, well leaded, with a restrained display cut for the folio cover and course of names. Nothing decorative, no script, no drop shadow.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, the voice of a caption card rather than a scrapbook. Example line the brand would write: "Ada Hollis, Brattleboro, 1912. Studio card portrait."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files. What survives is nine home flatbed scans, the daughter's catalogue and notes, and the Brattleboro framer's 2019 press PDF for the caption cards, of which six are already on the wall. The framer has retired, so the new cards must match his file rather than a live template.
brand_identity.values: Identity is the whole point: whatever is really in the photograph stays in the photograph, and nothing is invented or tidied away.

task_name: Gable and Grove - Home services before-and-after library
client_brief:
Before-and-after renovation photographs that clients can trust

Gable & Grove needs five before-and-after pairs prepared for the website and sales materials. These are evidence of our work. The after pictures should look good, but not because the before pictures have been made deliberately worse.

What we need back
- Completed project case-study panel: 4 named exports. The before and after photographs show the same site. The comparison preserves meaningful structural differences. The project caption identifies the work actually shown.
- Estimate-pack cover: 1 named export. The cover identifies Gable and Grove. The selected project demonstrates the service without claiming an invented result.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Premium exterior renovation and garden build for old houses, sold job by job at the kitchen table.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A five person firm working the Litchfield Hills of Connecticut, owner led, running full exterior renovations and garden builds.
brand_identity.about: Gable & Grove takes on full exterior renovations and garden builds between roughly 45,000 and 120,000 dollars a project. Everything is sold twice, once on the website and once out of a quote pack on somebody's kitchen table, so the work has to look like exactly what the firm delivers and no more. The proof is the before and after, and the before has to stay honest.
brand_identity.audience: Households aged 45 to 65 with old houses and long time horizons, choosing between two or three bids and buying on trust rather than on price.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 45,000 to 120,000 dollars a project. At this band the finish reads cool, calm and material: real neutral stone, deep honest blacks, one photograph doing the work, generous white space, and a mark that behaves like a maker's stamp rather than a sales badge. Never a supermarket flyer, never developer marketing.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet display serif for the mark and headings paired with a restrained humanist sans for scope, prices and captions. Legible, unhurried, no starbursts and no oversized phone number.
brand_identity.voice: Plain and confident, the voice of a builder who does not oversell. Example line the brand would write: "Full exterior renovation, Ridge Road. Limestone pergola, dry stone terrace, planting."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark is a problem the firm names openly: the sign writer who drew it is gone, and all that survives is a picture file he emailed once and a photograph of the mark hand painted on the firm's truck door. The project cards survive only as the retired printer's press PDF. Yard signs print in the deep Grove Green.
brand_identity.values: Honest befores are non negotiable, and the finish should read as ordered restraint rather than as an improved photograph.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Meridian Motors - Showroom vehicle image system
client_brief:
Standardise a used-car photo set without changing the cars

We photograph stock in three different bays at Meridian Motors. That is showing up in our listings: the same forecourt can look like three dealerships, and paint colours move around with the light.

The commission

 Vehicle sales card: 6 named exports. The vehicle photograph matches this stock record. The vehicle condition is not misrepresented by retouching. The enquiry action is readable.

 Forecourt inventory campaign: 1 named export. The dealership name is clear. The campaign uses vehicles present in the intake register.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Certified pre-owned car dealership taking roughly six vehicles a week onto the lot.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: An independent certified pre-owned dealership in Portland, Maine, photographing every car in house across three lot bays.
brand_identity.about: Meridian Motors sells certified pre-owned vehicles between 22,000 and 38,000 dollars to families replacing an ageing car. The listings are the whole business, and the visual argument is simple: this is an orderly operation with nothing to hide. Every car should look as if it were photographed in one clean, evenly lit showroom, with honest paint and legible plain information.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 replacing a ten year old family car, deciding on trust before they decide on the vehicle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 22,000 to 38,000 dollars certified pre-owned. The treatment is an even, neutral, well lit showroom white with the full vehicle in frame and honest colour. Never a dark dramatic studio look, which reads as evasive at this price, and never hot saturated pictures with starbursts and a price slash, which read as a buy here pay here lot.
brand_identity.typography: A clear humanist sans doing most of the work, sized so a price and a mileage read at a glance, with a slightly firmer cut for the roundel wordmark. Organised and plainly legible, neither luxury nor discount.
brand_identity.voice: Straightforward and unadorned, the voice of a desk that states the facts. Example line the brand would write: "2017 Calder Kestrel, 68,400 miles. Certified. 24,900 dollars."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only mark on file is the compass roundel as the sign shop supplied it years ago, a small flat raster on a white square at signage thumbnail size, which has never mattered until now. The window cards survive only as the retired printer's press PDF, and the room now hand writes them. The roundel belongs on the firm's own collateral and never on a marketplace primary.
brand_identity.values: Order and honesty above effect: the listing is the vehicle a buyer will walk around in person, so it must show the real car, plainly.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: OSTRA - Restaurant plate photography system
client_brief:
OSTRA tasting-menu images: dark, precise and still appetising

OSTRA is a 22-seat tasting counter. We have thirteen plate photographs from two services, and we need them to feel like the same room and the same menu. Dark should not mean muddy; glaze and food texture still need to read.

Deliverables
1. Seasonal menu announcement: 1 named export. OSTRA is identified. The featured dish agrees with the seasonal menu. The reservation action is visible.
2. Booking-page dish tile: 13 named exports. The caption correctly identifies the pictured dish. The food is recognisable at mobile listing size.
3. Reservation story: 1 named export. The booking action sits within the defined safe area. The restaurant name is readable at mobile size.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A contemporary seasonal tasting counter, twenty two seats around the pass, one menu a night, four nights a week.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A twenty two seat tasting counter on the coast of New England, one seasonal menu at 135 dollars a head served four nights a week.
brand_identity.about: OSTRA is a counter, not a dining room: guests sit around the pass for one seasonal tasting menu at 135 dollars a head. The room is near black, spare and unhurried, and the photography is meant to feel like walking into it rather than like an advertisement. One plate at a time, on a dark ground, with light that still reads as light.
brand_identity.audience: Guests aged 30 to 55 booking an occasion around six weeks ahead, who expect calm and consideration rather than volume.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A 135 dollar seasonal tasting counter. The grammar is a near black ground, one plate per frame, generous emptiness, restrained saturation, and speculars on sauce and glass that read as light rather than as blown white or flat grey. Never a bright, crowded bistro look, and never near monochrome art photography in which the food cannot be read.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet editorial serif for course titles and guest names paired with a minimal sans for detail lines, set light on a near black ground. Spare and considered, neither bistro chalkboard nor hotel gilt.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and understated, the voice of a room that lets the plate speak. Example line the brand would write: "Five courses. One seating. Please arrive as the light goes."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no editable brand files. The per guest menu card survives only as the old printer's press PDF, and the printer has been lost, so the room hand writes about forty cards a night. A dark mode site reference screengrab was supplied as mood only, and course titles come spelled as the kitchen spells them.
brand_identity.values: Honesty of the room and one plate at a time: the photographs are this kitchen's real plates, and restraint is what the guest is paying for.

Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Northgrove - Apparel colorway image system
client_brief:
Colour-consistent apparel images and clean retailer cutouts

Our Northgrove range is affordable premium basics. Customers choose between colours and fabrics, so a polished set that changes either of those is not useful to us.

Please prepare
- Apparel style product-page module: 6 named exports. The garment geometry matches its source style. The colourway is identified accurately. Fabric texture survives the treatment.
- Capsule launch carousel: 6 named exports. The capsule has a coherent visual direction. The opening page identifies Northgrove. The closing page contains the approved shopping action.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Better than it looks in the price.
brand_identity.sector: Elevated basics apparel: a six style seasonal capsule sold direct online and through one marketplace feed, including a supporters' crew made with a local amateur football club.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Burlington, Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Northgrove is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Burlington, Vermont, and this commission covers phase 1: apparel colour and ecommerce proofing.
brand_identity.audience: Women and men aged 22 to 38 choosing on a phone, cross shopping against a 9 dollar fast fashion tee and a 140 dollar heritage one, buying a 32 to 60 dollar piece they expect to keep.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Elevated basics at 32 to 60 dollars. We sit above fast fashion and below heritage. The whole proposition is that the cloth is better than the price suggests, so nothing may read as cheaper or as more luxury than the parcel actually is.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a charcoal condensed sans set tight for the wordmark; text in a calm humanist sans with generous leading. The feel is plain and confident, never editorial, never bold discount.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, a little dry. We name the cloth and the cut and leave the adjectives out. Example line the brand would write: 'Loopback cotton, dyed in small lots, made to soften with wear.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our olive leaf glyph and charcoal wordmark only survive as a picture lifted off an old lookbook page. The studio that drew them has closed and no one has the source file, so the mark needs recovering as real artwork before it can go on cards or launch pieces.
brand_identity.values: Honesty between the picture and the product, and small batch cloth that earns its price.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
Color variants are approval concepts until physical samples are photographed and signed off.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

1600 px transparent raster companion for placement and preview.
White vector variant for approved dark-ground use.
1600 px transparent white raster variant.

task_name: Lumora - Lip oil shade concept set
client_brief:
Lip-oil shade concepts for a launch that has one physical sample

Important before you quote: Lumora has one physical lip-oil sample, not seven approved production shades. This is concept-colour work. Every result must say CONCEPT COLOR - SAMPLE APPROVAL REQUIRED.

Final handoff

 Retailer shade card: 8 named exports. The bottle keeps the approved packaging geometry. The concept-colour notice is readable. The displayed shade agrees with its shade name.

 Seven-shade comparison: 1 named export. The seven approved shade names are present. The shades appear in the approved range order. The concept-colour notice is readable.

 Lip oil product-page module: 1 named export. The product name is accurate. The benefit uses the approved claim wording. The concept-colour notice is readable.

 Lip oil launch feed ad: 1 named export. Lumora is identified. The call to action is readable at mobile size. The product edge has no visible halo. The concept-colour notice is readable.

 Lip oil launch story: 1 named export. The headline is readable at mobile size. The call to action remains within the safe area. The concept-colour notice is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Every shade concept must show CONCEPT COLOR - SAMPLE APPROVAL REQUIRED. Only Amber Hour is the physical-sample reference.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer colour cosmetics: one lip oil launching in a seven shade range, sold shade first on mobile with a small retailer feed alongside.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Los Angeles, California; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Lumora is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Los Angeles, California, and this commission covers phase 1: pre-production lip-oil colour concepts.
brand_identity.audience: 18 to 32 year olds discovering us on social and buying shade first on a phone, cross shopping a 6 dollar drugstore oil and a 38 dollar prestige one.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A 24 dollar lip oil. We want to look more expensive than we are while staying honest, so the treatment is bright, clean and daylight neutral, never moody prestige and never blown out drugstore.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a clean confident sans with a little character; text in a neutral daylight sans. The feel is fresh and self assured, neither serif prestige nor bold discount.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, a bit fun, never overclaiming. We describe the finish and let the shade speak. Example line the brand would write: 'A sheer wash of colour, a proper shine, no stickiness.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark and shade lockups exist as working digital files. There is no printed guideline; the carton photograph we have was shot under shop light and should not be trusted as a colour reference.
brand_identity.values: That the shade on the screen is the shade on the lip, and that a launch can look premium without pretending to be prestige.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
Color variants are approval concepts until physical samples are photographed and signed off.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Kilnmore - Ceramic ecommerce image system
client_brief:
A coherent ceramics range, with the glaze differences left intact

We sell the surface as much as the form at Kilnmore. Fourteen pieces and their glaze details need to become one usable product image library, but the work should not flatten the glazes into the same colour or texture.

Scope
1. Ceramic product-page module: 14 named exports. The vessel geometry matches the named product. The glaze retains its material texture.
2. Wholesale range one-sheet: 1 named export. The range names agree with the supplied register. Trade information is easy to scan.
3. Ceramic range launch carousel: 5 named exports. Kilnmore is identified on the opening page. The range sequence makes product differences clear.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Matte glaze stoneware: a two person studio selling direct, through a national handmade marketplace, and on consignment in six independent shops.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Portland, Maine; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Kilnmore is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Portland, Maine, and this commission covers phase 1: ecommerce product image system.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 who buy craft and buy a specific glaze, reading the piece and its finish before they order.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Considered handmade stoneware at 38 to 95 dollars a piece. Above mass import homeware, below gallery ceramics. The house look is neutral and airy with the glaze true to the piece in the hand, never punchy and saturated, never near black gallery styling.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a quiet humanist serif with real craft warmth; text in a plain grotesque set with generous air. The feel is considered and calm, neither rustic cute nor gallery austere.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grounded, specific about material and process. We name the glaze, the form and the firing and stop there. Example line the brand would write: 'Wheel thrown stoneware, matte celadon, oxidised recesses left dark.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only clean copy of our mark left is the printed wrapping tissue we wrap orders in. The wordmark and enclosed kiln arch device need recovering from that photograph as placeable artwork; there is no source file.
brand_identity.values: Truth to the glaze in the buyer's hand, and the craft of small batch stoneware.

task_name: Argent and Faith - Spring jewelry capsule photography
client_brief:
Silver jewellery retouching with an honest plan for open centres

Argent & Faith needs ten seasonal pieces prepared as a consistent listing set. The silver should read as silver, with a common light and scale across the range. We do not want the high polish turned into featureless grey.

What we need back
- Jewellery capsule campaign poster: 1 named export. The jewellery remains the primary visual focus. The campaign identifies Argent and Faith.
- Jewellery product detail: 10 named exports. The stone setting matches the named piece. Metal colour remains believable.
- Retailer capsule look sheet: 1 named export. Product labels identify the pictured pieces. The layout communicates the capsule relationship.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Let the metal do the work.
brand_identity.sector: Independent silver jewellery studio: a two bench workshop putting out a ten piece capsule each season, sold direct and through eleven independent stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, a two bench silver studio in Providence, Rhode Island, run by two makers.
brand_identity.about: Argent & Faith is a two bench silver studio. Nora cuts and pierces, her partner finishes and sets, and we put out ten considered pieces a season: open bands, a pierced medallion, a signet, a reliquary locket. We sell direct and through eleven independent shops. The negative space in a band or a piercing is the design, so how a piece is made and photographed matters as much as what it costs.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 28 to 55, Northeast urban and coastal, buying one considered piece for themselves or as a milestone gift and reading the metal and dimensions before purchase.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fine but accessible silver at 180 to 900 dollars a piece. Above high street silver, below designer gallery jewellery. At this tier the tile is mostly air, the piece sits small and centred, the type is quiet and provenance reads as editorial copy.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a refined high contrast serif with quiet authority; text in a clean neutral sans set small with air. The feel is considered and editorial, the metal leading and the type receding.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, precise, provenance led. We write in Nora's own plain words about how a piece was made. Example line the brand would write: 'Hand sawn and pierced, sterling silver, oxidised and hand finished at the bench.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our maker's mark exists only as an engraving in the steel bench block Nora's teacher cut for her, and nowhere else. There is no file and no one to ask, so the mark needs recovering from a photograph as artwork that stays true to the original rather than a tidier version of it.
brand_identity.values: Honest metal and honest making, and negative space treated as the design rather than a gap.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Girdermark - Industrial component image system
client_brief:
Catalogue-ready component photography, including difficult internal openings

Girdermark sells replacement components. A buyer needs to recognise the finish and the shape, not admire a dramatic studio treatment. Our twelve components were photographed over two bench sessions and need a consistent technical presentation.

The commission

 Industrial SKU plate: 12 named exports. The part geometry agrees with the source component. Surface defects affecting identification remain visible.

 Industrial SKU cutout: 12 named exports. The silhouette preserves all functional holes. The edge has no visible halo.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The number and the part agree.
brand_identity.sector: Industrial and Manufacturing, wholesale distribution of elevator and electrical replacement parts
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Cleveland, Ohio; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Girdermark Elevator & Electrical Supply is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Cleveland, Ohio, and this commission covers phase 1: components photography and technical sheets.
brand_identity.audience: Working buyers aged 35 to 60 who have specified this class of part for twenty years and judge a supplier by whether the photography and the spec table say the same thing. They order by part number and hold us to the values printed beside it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid to upper industrial. Parts run 400 to 9,000 dollars. The material has to read as trustworthy and technical, never as a consumer hardware brand and never as glossy marketing.
brand_identity.typography: A single clear grotesque for headings and part numbers, a plain, generously set text face for the long spec tables. Nothing decorative. Numbers must be legible at a glance and unmistakable one from another.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, factual, no adjectives we cannot stand behind. We state the number, the finish and the price and we stop. If something is wrong we say so before it prints.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We have no working brand files and no written guidelines. Our data sheets exist only as a flat press PDF the printer sent us last spring, and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep that sheet exactly as our customers recognise it. The palette and type notes above are our best account of the look, reconstructed for you, not a formal system.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over polish. Availability. Honesty about what we stock and what a part will do. We would rather lose a sale than print a spec we cannot certify.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Summit and Sable - Recovery-gear launch campaign
client_brief:
Recovery-gear image system with a controlled Ridge Blue colourway

We need Summit & Sable's field and bench photographs to read as one recovery-gear range. There are twenty supplied captures, with webbing, stitching and hardware that need to remain convincing at close range.

Deliverables
1. Recovery-gear launch poster: 1 named export. The actual Summit and Sable equipment is shown. The poster contains no unsupported safety claim.
2. Recovery equipment product-page module: 9 named exports. The component geometry matches the named equipment. The load or use wording matches supplied approved copy.
3. Recovery-gear dealer sheet: 1 named export. The range is clearly identified. Specifications are readable at print size.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Gear that looks like it works.
brand_identity.sector: E-commerce and retail, value-band recovery and overlanding gear
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Boulder, Colorado. Small owner-run shop, under ten people, selling on a marketplace and its own storefront.
brand_identity.about: We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit for people with a lifted truck and a real budget. Nine SKUs from 35 to 220 dollars. Our buyer is not paying for a name, he is paying because the gear looks like it will hold when he is stuck at dusk on a fire road. The detail is the whole argument: the stitching and the hardware finish are what separate us from the cheap import sitting next to us in search results.
brand_identity.audience: Off-road and 4x4 owners aged 25 to 50, buying on rugged credibility and price. They trust flat daylight and visible workmanship and they distrust anything that looks staged or expensive.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Value band, 35 to 220 dollars. The look is bright, hard-wearing and legible, honest daylight on the plain-ground shots and unstyled dust on the field shots. Never premium-expedition cinematic, never discount-banner loud. Either extreme reads as pretending and loses the buyer.
brand_identity.typography: Type should read as workwear signage: a sturdy condensed or grotesque for headlines and spec callouts, a clean neutral text face for body and the range table. Bold but balanced, plenty of negative space, nothing magazine-like.
brand_identity.voice: Blunt and plain. We say what the gear does and what it is rated for. Certified working loads are stated as certified and never rounded or dressed up.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only brand mark file we can find is a flat screen-size export our old developer left us, plus a photo of the same mark on a woven label. We have no scalable artwork and no written guidelines. Charcoal is our storefront ground and Ridge Blue is the new webbing colour we are introducing. Treat the notes above as direction, not a locked system.
brand_identity.values: Honesty in the picture and the spec. Durability over shine. Fair price for real capability. If an edit would make the product look like something it is not, we would rather it stayed plain.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: SlabVault - Collectible card marketplace image system
client_brief:
Consignment listing photographs where the holder and label remain legible

SlabVault handles graded collectibles. A listing photograph has to show the item and the evidence around it: holder, label and seal. Glare is a problem in the current set, but we cannot replace unreadable information with a convincing guess.

Please prepare
- Collectible listing front: 14 named exports. The card identity matches the lot. Condition defects remain visible.
- Collectible condition detail: 14 named exports. The holder details are legible. The photograph does not imply a different grade.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Graded with confidence, sold with proof
brand_identity.sector: Graded-collectible consignment (trading cards and comics)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Providence, Rhode Island; a four person consignment house
brand_identity.about: SlabVault Cards is a small consignment house that lists and settles graded collectibles for private sellers. Lots run from roughly 150 to 5,000 dollars per item, and buyers decide from the photograph alone, zooming into the holder, the label and the corners before they bid. Consignors shoot their own slabs on their own tables, so the house exists to bring many different rooms to one credible standard. Trust is the entire product: everything SlabVault presents has to read as accurate, unretouched and verifiable.
brand_identity.audience: Condition-literate collectors aged 25 to 60 who buy graded cards and comics at 150 to 5,000 dollars a lot, read the grade and certification line straight out of the image, and walk away from anything that looks staged or concealed.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid to upper consignment. Not a bulk reseller or a toy shop, and not a fine-art auction room. The presentation sits deliberately between the two: neutral, generous and evidential, never cheap and flashy, never gilded and theatrical.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, legible pairing: a humanist sans for body copy and roster data, and a slightly firmer grotesque or restrained slab for lot numbers and headings. Type stays small, even and confident. No decorative or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, factual, collector to collector. States the grade, the grader and the condition without hype. Never breathless, never salesy. The photograph does the persuading.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: SlabVault has never held a proper brand kit. What exists is a house note describing the palette in words (grey, black, one amber accent already used on the printed stationery and the sleeve ticket), the grading partner names spelled the way the graders require, and the sale details. There is no logo file, no type specimen and no template, so the house look has to be established fresh and held consistently across the listings, the printed tickets and the auction-week set.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over polish. Show the item exactly as submitted, give every slab room to be read, and never add an edge, shine or shadow that was not there. The buyer's confidence is the asset the whole business protects.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
An obscured grading or compliance label must be rejected for reshoot, not reconstructed from guesswork.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Continental Cup - Player portrait card system
client_brief:
Eight-player card run with matched portraits and checked player identities

Continental Cup needs the eight-player release prepared from the supplied portraits and roster. The pictures come from two stadium lighting rigs; the cards come from a printer's PDF we need to make usable again.

Final handoff

 Player press card: 9 named exports. The portrait belongs to the named player. The player number is legible. The competition identity is visible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The set every fan wants sealed
brand_identity.sector: Officially licensed sports collector cards (continental club football tournament)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: touring competition, Western Europe and North America; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Continental Cup 2026 Collector Card Programme is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is touring competition, Western Europe and North America, and this commission covers phase 1: collector-card portrait finishing.
brand_identity.audience: Collectors aged 16 to 45 who buy officially licensed cup sets, know a licensed release from a fan-made one at a glance, and expect deep, saturated, high-contrast presentation worthy of a marquee tournament.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium licensed collector tier. Pack twelve dollars, sealed box ninety-five, featured cards trading roughly 30 to 120 dollars secondary. The treatment is deep and saturated with real floodlit blacks, one dominant player per card, type set large and confident. Never a flat, bright community-league sheet, and never a neon gaming poster.

palette.name: Pitch Deep Navy (retailer display and card field)

brand_identity.typography: A confident licensed-sport system: a strong condensed or wide display face for player names and the set masthead, paired with a clean, sturdy sans for squad numbers, position, honours line and data. Numerals must read cleanly at small card sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Bold, official and celebratory without slang. Speaks with the authority of a sanctioned tournament: it names the players, states the honours and lets the floodlit imagery carry the drama.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The brand files are largely lost. The studio that designed last year's card has closed, and all that survives is the flat file the printer ran, whose layout the retailers already recognise and want kept. The competition crest was never held as artwork at all: the only reference is a daylight photograph of the embroidered patch on an official's sleeve. The recovered mark and the rebuilt card layout therefore have to be reconstructed from those remnants and carried forward as the programme's working assets.
brand_identity.values: Authenticity of the licence above all. Depict the real featured players and the real competition mark faithfully, print the licensing copy exactly as supplied, and hold one premium look across print and store so the set reads as sanctioned, not imitated.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Fernwell and Rowe - Hartley wedding gallery finishing
client_brief:
Wedding retouching pilot: one warm house look across changing light

We are Fernwell & Rowe, and this is a pilot using the Hartley wedding shortlist. There are sixteen photographs spanning window light, golden hour and the reception. We want a natural warm treatment that holds together through those changes without giving every person the same skin colour.

Scope
1. Wedding review image: 16 named exports. The people retain their source identities. Skin retains natural texture. The scene remains faithful to the event.
2. Full-resolution wedding keeper: 6 named exports. The keeper matches the explicitly supplied selection. Highlight detail is retained where present in the source.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: A real day, warm and honest
brand_identity.sector: A two-person wedding and event photography studio in the Cotswolds shooting full-day coverage for couples marrying at country-house venues.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, the Cotswolds, England, a two-photographer studio where the two partners shoot together and share every edit.
brand_identity.about: Fernwell & Rowe photograph twenty-two weddings a season across Cotswolds country-house venues. Two people run everything, from the first walk-through to the finished gallery, and they promise couples a record of the actual day rather than a styled magazine shoot. These prints sit on parents' walls for thirty years, so the work stays warm, natural and true to skin.
brand_identity.audience: Couples aged 27 to 38 booking a Cotswolds country-house venue eighteen months out and paying for full-day coverage; their parents will look at the prints for decades.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Full-day coverage 3,200 to 5,500 pounds, a mid-to-upper independent band. Above the filtered budget packages, below glossy editorial studios. The finish should feel like a real day, not a preset and not a phone filter.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet book-weight serif for names and headings, warm and traditional rather than fashion-led, set against a plain humanist sans for dates and captions. Nothing glossy.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain and first person plural, the two of them talking to a couple. Example line: We would rather pull a frame and tell you than force it.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The studio has no working brand files. The thank-you card survives only as the press PDF the printer ran, the designer who made it two years ago is no longer reachable, and the wax seal the studio presses on every envelope has never existed as a file, only as a photograph of one pressed seal.
brand_identity.values: A real day honestly recorded, and skin that stays true across every light of the day.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Cascadia Founders Summit - Executive portrait set
client_brief:
Conference speaker portraits from eighteen very different submissions

Our Cascadia Founders Summit speakers have sent their own photographs. They need to sit together in the programme, in tight squares and on wide stage screens. Please make them look like one event without making the people look alike.

What we need back
- Summit speaker card: 18 named exports. The portrait belongs to the named speaker. The role is readable at mobile size. The summit identity is visible.
- Summit announcement: 1 named export. The event name is clear. The approved date is visible. The registration action is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

brand_identity.tagline: Founders and the people who fund them
brand_identity.sector: A paid two-day founders summit in Portland, Oregon, for founders, operators and institutional investors.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Portland, Oregon, now in its second edition, run by a core team of four staff for a room of about four hundred.
brand_identity.about: Cascadia Founders Summit is a two-day gathering for founders and the people who back them. Passes run six hundred to twelve hundred dollars and the room is roughly four hundred people who read the calibre of the event off its details. The summit sells seriousness and access rather than spectacle, and everything it puts in front of that audience is meant to look considered.
brand_identity.audience: Founders, operators and institutional investors aged 28 to 55 who expense the ticket and judge the event by how professional it feels.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Delegate passes 600 to 1,200 dollars, a credible professional summit priced above a free meetup and below a flagship conference. Restraint reads as calibre; a glossy or busy treatment would misprice it.
brand_identity.typography: A restrained contemporary serif for titles paired with a clean neutral sans for names, role lines and body copy. Even and quiet, with no display flourish.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, direct and professional, confident without selling hard. Example line: Passes are limited and the room is small on purpose.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The summit builds its own website and needs no pages. Its badge artwork exists only as the press PDF the venue printer ran last year, with no working file behind it. The house ground, mark and tone are described in the brand notes rather than handed over as a kit.
brand_identity.values: A serious room worth the price of admission, where credibility is read off the smallest details.

task_name: Astrid Vellacourt - Editorial portrait session
client_brief:
A coherent speaking and investor image set for an industrial-design founder

I am preparing speaking and investor materials for Astrid Vellacourt. The photographs and supporting pieces need to feel like the same person and practice: considered, credible and recognisably connected to industrial design.

The commission

 Speaker booking one-pager: 1 named export. The biography preserves approved facts. The talk offer is clear. The booking contact is readable.

 Event-specific speaker announcement: 1 named export. The event name is visible. The event date matches the supplied talk record. The speaker name is clear.

 Speaker event banner: 1 named export. The banner identifies the specific talk. The speaker portrait is recognisable.

 Speaker talk card: 9 named exports. The talk title matches this record. The event identity is visible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: The founder personal brand of the co-founder and managing director of Vellacourt & Sund, a six-person industrial design studio, during a seed raise and a European speaking season.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Studio Vellacourt & Sund founded 2019 in Europe, six people; the personal brand is Astrid's own, built for a seed round and three conference talks between February and May.
brand_identity.about: Astrid Vellacourt co-founded and runs Vellacourt & Sund, a six-person industrial design studio. Her personal brand exists for the season when her face is in front of investors and programme committees who do not yet know her. It has to read as a person who runs a company, composed and credible, never as an influencer or an account, because she is asking for money and for stage time.
brand_identity.audience: Institutional investors, conference programme committees and prospective senior hires; Astrid is between 30 and 50.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Founder personal-brand package 900 to 1,800 dollars, pitched at institutional level. Neither an over-filtered influencer treatment nor a stiff corporate flash-on-white; understated is the point.
brand_identity.typography: A modern serif with an industrial-design sensibility for her name and the monogram lockup, set with a precise neutral sans for supporting text. Restrained rather than luxury-glossy.
brand_identity.voice: First person, plain and self-possessed. Example line: I want it to look like someone who runs a company, not someone who runs an account.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no brand kit. The AV monogram exists only as a blind deboss pressed into an old studio card, with no file and the printer closed, surviving only as a photograph of the impression. The warm ground she wants and the dark ground her press kit uses are described in her placement notes rather than supplied as artwork.
brand_identity.values: Work that reads as a design studio founder at institutional level, with her own mark used quietly and her likeness kept honest.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
