task_name: Quill and Kiln - Autumn ceramics signature look
client_brief:
An autumn image library that still looks like my ceramics

Hi, I am Marlo Quill, the maker behind Quill & Kiln. I have a month's worth of photographs from my phone and a borrowed camera, taken under four different kinds of light. I need help turning them into a usable autumn collection.

Deliverables
1. Autumn studio journal carousel: 6 named exports. The image sequence tells a coherent making story. The captions match the pictured work.
2. Studio journal feature: 1 named export. The typography supports an editorial reading order. The feature identifies Quill and Kiln.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: A real person in a real studio
brand_identity.sector: An independent maker and lifestyle creator in Portland selling small-batch stoneware, with a seasonal coffee-bar collaboration each autumn.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Quill and Kiln, founded 2020, Portland, Oregon, a one-maker studio working from a shared space, with roughly nine thousand followers.
brand_identity.about: Marlo Quill makes small-batch stoneware in a shared Portland studio and sells it four times a year, plus a coffee-bar collaboration each autumn. About a third of what she sells comes straight off her own posts. The brand is the person: a real maker in a real room, warm and quiet, and never a polished label, because that is what her audience follows her for.
brand_identity.audience: Followers aged 22 to 34, the same age as Marlo, who buy 38 to 90 dollar stoneware and follow the maker rather than a brand.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A mid-tier creator retainer of 600 to 1,500 dollars a month, stoneware at 38 to 90 dollars. Above careless untreated phone photos, below gallery-ceramics gloss; a heavy uniform filter would read as selling out and cost her directly.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist serif with a hand feel for names and headings, paired with a simple unfussy sans for captions and prices. A maker's hand rather than an agency deck.
brand_identity.voice: First person, casual and direct. Example line: One look, mine, not a filter.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No formal brand files. Her three motifs, a mug, a sprig and a small kiln, exist only as ink on a photographed sketchbook page she keeps re-cropping. The true glaze colours are pinned by a single reference frame of fired test tiles rather than any spec, and there is no logo file.
brand_identity.values: One recognisable hand across the whole feed, with real rooms, true glaze colours and her own drawn marks.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Nordhaven - Harbour hotel booking campaign
client_brief:
Give a small harbour hotel a distinct look without losing room accuracy

Nordhaven occupies a harbour warehouse with fourteen rooms. We want a distinctive image treatment for the brand, while keeping one room hero true to colour so guests can see what they are booking.

Please prepare
- Harbour hotel booking hero: 1 named export. The scene is the supplied Nordhaven property. The booking action is clear.
- Hotel amenity panel: 1 named export. The named amenities are supported by the source pack. The information is easy to scan.
- Hotel room campaign: 14 named exports. The room photograph matches this room category. The advertised rate preserves its supplied conditions.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: A room with the harbour in it
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen-room design-led micro-hotel in a converted harbour warehouse, sold direct.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opened 2023 on the Nordhavn waterfront, Copenhagen; fourteen rooms run by one small owner-led team.
brand_identity.about: Nordhaven is a fourteen-room hotel inside a converted brick and timber warehouse on the working harbour. We sell the feeling of the building: cold light, plaster, oak and brass. Guests choose us because the place looks like nowhere else, and everything we make has to carry that.
brand_identity.audience: Design-literate urban travellers, 30 to 45, who choose a property on aesthetic and book direct once they trust the point of view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Six hundred dollars a night, direct only, positioned above the travel-platform grid as a design destination rather than a room count.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high-contrast serif for display, set large and used sparingly, with a clean neutral grotesque for text. Nothing shouts, and rates sit small.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, understated, first person, no exclamation. Example line: 'Fourteen rooms on the water. We open direct booking this autumn.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We work from a short brand note that fixes the near-black ground, the placements and the delivered sizes. There is no full guideline system yet, and the room list changes each season.
brand_identity.values: One committed tone across everything, with the true-colour main room photograph kept as the single deliberate exception so guests see the actual bed and linen.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Ironline Forge - Blacksmith editorial image set
client_brief:
Foundry photographs for architects: one dark treatment, visible material

The furnace and rooflight give us two very different versions of Ironline Forge. We need an experienced retoucher to bring them together for architectural audiences and the expo.

Final handoff

 Architectural foundry editorial feature: 1 named export. The sequence explains the foundry's casting work. Tool and material detail remains credible.

 Foundry exhibition poster: 1 named export. The architectural casting offer uses approved copy. The specifier contact is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A heritage iron and bronze foundry casting bespoke architectural work for specifiers and developers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Casting since 1911 in the same Sheffield works; a small crew of founders, patternmakers and finishers.
brand_identity.about: Ironline Forge casts bespoke iron and bronze for architects and developers who have mostly never stood on a foundry floor. We sell permanence and provenance: the heat, the hands, and the fact that the piece will still be here in eighty years. The brand has to feel like the shop floor, hot, dirty and precise.
brand_identity.audience: Specifiers, architects and developers, 40 to 65, buying craft and confidence rather than a catalogue product.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bespoke castings from five to sixty thousand dollars a piece, priced on provenance and never presented as a promotion.
brand_identity.typography: A generous editorial serif for headlines with plenty of black around it, and a strong grotesque for labels and spec lines. Numbers are set plainly.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, declarative, unshowy. Example line: 'Iron and bronze, cast in this building since 1911.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our maker's mark was cut into a die generations ago and survives only struck into the metal. There is no artwork for it anywhere, and the trade-fair stand and the brand story page are being rebuilt at the same time.
brand_identity.values: Process and provenance over polish. The struck maker's mark must be recovered faithfully rather than tidied into a fashion monoline, and it has to hold small and reversed out of the dark.

task_name: Lunara Chronometry - Autumn watch campaign
client_brief:
Watch campaign treatment plus colour-accurate dealer product files

Two kinds of files are needed for Lunara Chronometry, and they must not be confused. The campaign can carry our tonal treatment; the dealer needs clean product files, including a dial-finish reference that stays true to colour.

Scope
1. Autumn watch key visual: 1 named export. The watch dial matches the approved reference. The watch remains the dominant visual.
2. Watch product-page feature: 5 named exports. The case geometry matches the named watch. The specification wording is accurate.
3. Watch dealer launch sheet: 1 named export. Model identities are unambiguous. The layout reflects the stated price position.

brand_identity.tagline: Timed by hand, one at a time
brand_identity.sector: An independent mechanical watch house making five references in small runs, sold direct and through two dealers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A studio of eight in Chicago, Illinois; a Swiss-trained watchmaker and a regulator who times every piece by hand.
brand_identity.about: Lunara builds mechanical watches in small runs and regulates each one by hand before it ships. We sell presence, finish and the credibility of a named regulator, not a colour or a trend. Every piece leaves with its own certificate, and the pictures have to read as confidence.
brand_identity.audience: Collector-literate buyers, 35 to 60, who judge a watch on form, finish and the hand behind it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Four to twelve thousand dollars a piece, positioned as independent horology: above fashion watchmaking and below the grand houses.
brand_identity.typography: A refined serif with small caps for the wordmark and reference names, and a neat grotesque for specifications. The certificate reads formal and calm.
brand_identity.voice: Exact, understated, collector to collector. Example line: 'Five references. Each one regulated by hand and signed.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We have last season's certificate as it went to the printer and an approved wording note. The timing line is fixed and cannot be reworded, and the featured reference moves each season.
brand_identity.values: One committed warm single-tone treatment with fine grain across the whole campaign, with a single true-colour dial frame kept so a customer can judge the finish honestly.

task_name: Apexguard - Industrial surfaces launch photography
client_brief:
Apexguard imagery and recovered logo for a tightly defined six-SKU release

Release scope: six product SKUs
- V-PPF-104, V-PPF-105 and V-PPF-107
- U-TNT-204 and U-TNT-208
- F-HW-301

What we need back
- Industrial surfaces dealer poster: 1 named export. The correct Apexguard sub-brand is used. The advertised application is supported by source imagery.
- Surface product-page module: 6 named exports. The product variant is identified accurately. The surface finish retains its source texture.
- Sub-brand application sheet: 1 named export. The sub-brand hierarchy is clear. The approved master lettering is preserved.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Built to sit behind the counter
brand_identity.sector: An automotive aftermarket supplier of paint protection film, window tint and installation hardware, sold to independent installers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Charlotte, North Carolina; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Apexguard is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Charlotte, North Carolina, and this commission covers phase 1: rebrand photography and product rollout.
brand_identity.audience: Independent installers, 25 to 45, who judge a supplier on whether the packaging justifies the price to a customer standing at the counter.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Line items from two hundred fifty to twelve hundred dollars, a confident premium supplier rather than a bright discount accessory brand.
brand_identity.typography: A tight modern grotesque, mostly caps, with wide tracking on the master mark. Fitment and warranty lines are set plainly and stay legible at small size.
brand_identity.voice: Confident and terse, no hype. Example line: 'Film, tint and hardware. Fitted right, backed properly.' No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our master mark survives only on a die-cut box sticker and on a decal on an installer's shop glass. The studio that drew it has closed and taken the source files, so it has to be recovered as usable artwork.
brand_identity.values: A dark, high-contrast house system with one accent, where fitment information is always legible on the shelf. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Thornmere Home - Autumn interiors image system
client_brief:
Wholesale product images that keep indigo and reactive glaze honest

Our homeware photographs were made under two lighting rigs. Thornmere needs the twenty ceramic and textile pieces to work as a range, both in retailer tiles and on a coloured wholesale band.

The commission

 Autumn interiors collection spread: 1 named export. The textiles preserve their source patterns. The styled grouping feels coherent.

 Interiors wholesale presentation: 1 named export. Each featured object has its correct product name. The page sequence supports a trade buying conversation.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Made by hand, kept for years.
brand_identity.sector: Mid-premium homeware: glazed stoneware and woven textiles
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded in Providence, Rhode Island. A two-person workshop selling direct to consumer and wholesale into fourteen independent stores across the Northeast.
brand_identity.about: Thornmere Home makes glazed stoneware and woven textiles in a small Providence workshop, around thirty-two products a season priced from forty-five to a hundred and eighty dollars. The work is honest material: real glaze, real dye, thrown and woven by people who sign for it. Ceramics are shot standing, textiles draped, and the range is meant to read as one quiet, warm family rather than a catalogue of individual objects. The season turns on autumn, when the palette deepens and the catalogue goes back to the printer, one product to a page.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly thirty to fifty who nest and furnish slowly. Design literate, buying to keep rather than to chase a trend. Neither farmhouse cliche nor design-gallery cool, just people who want warm, made things in the house.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-premium. Generous with white space, warm and truthful about material, never the austere near-black of collectible ceramics and never the crowded, saturated look of discount homeware.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif for product names and section headers, paired with a quiet grotesque for prices, dimensions and care lines. Restrained sizes, generous leading, plenty of air.
brand_identity.voice: Plain and warm. Short sentences about material and making, not about lifestyle. The maker writes the care lines and they stay in the maker's own words, unreworded.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand guidelines were ever written down. The autumn catalogue was built by an outside studio that has since closed and kept the working layout file, so only the printer's press PDF of the spring catalogue survives. The catalogue has to be rebuilt from that press PDF and the season's spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Truth to material, longevity over trend, and steady support of the independent stores that carry the range.

task_name: Fennhollow - Botanical soda summer campaign
client_brief:
Build a believable soda image set around two imperfect packshots

Fennhollow has two packshots that have already been pushed too far in retouching, and no lifestyle shoot. We need a product retoucher with a good eye for licensing compatible photography and for knowing when to stop correcting a damaged source.

Deliverables
1. Botanical soda summer key visual: 1 named export. The can artwork matches the approved product. The headline and can have a clear hierarchy.
2. Botanical ingredient carousel: 5 named exports. The featured ingredients match approved copy. The closing page contains the approved shopping action.
3. Soda retail display poster: 1 named export. The brand is visible at viewing size. The pack remains recognisable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Botanicals from the valley, nothing else.
brand_identity.sector: Craft botanical soda, better-for-you premium CPG
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded in the Hudson Valley, New York. Two founders working with a co-packer, three flavours, sold in upstate natural grocers and by direct-to-consumer subscription.
brand_identity.about: Fennhollow Botanical Soda makes three botanical sodas in the Hudson Valley: elderflower and lime, rhubarb and bitters, and spruce tip. Three dollars fifty a can, sold across upstate natural grocers and by subscription, produced through a co-packer whose cleared nutrition claim cannot be reworded. Two founders run everything and neither is a photographer. The whole brand lives on summer: sun lit, warm, natural, a little restrained. The spruce tip flavour steps to the front in August, so the summer campaign has to be built to be revisited as the season shifts.
brand_identity.audience: Twenty-five to forty, shopping the natural grocer aisle and reading the ingredient panel. Paying a premium for the promise that this is closer to a real thing than a mass soda.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Craft better-for-you at three fifty a can. Warmer and more human than a twelve-dollar apothecary tonic, and far more restrained and natural than a hyper-saturated ninety-nine-cent soda.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist sans across the family, legible over photography, paired with a friendly display cut for the flavour names. Natural and restrained, not wellness-minimal and not soda-aisle shout.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, a little rural. Names the botanicals and the valley, not a lifestyle. The co-packer's cleared claim line stays exactly as written.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No written brand guidelines have ever existed and the founders asked for the first one to be created. Their brand note points to a printed swatch card that was never sent with the package, so the house green survives only as the printed label on the two studio can shots the brand owns. There is no lifestyle photography of any kind.
brand_identity.values: Real ingredients over additives, provable and legal image provenance the co-packer can be shown, and a cohesive look the next hire can build on rather than start from nothing.

task_name: Verda Reformer Studio - Fitness campaign image system
client_brief:
A calm launch image system for a reformer studio with a limited shoot

Verda is a reformer studio, and the launch should feel calm, approachable and grounded in the room we actually have. Our two room photographs are dusky. We need them prepared alongside suitable licensed movement imagery, not replaced by a fictional studio.

Please prepare
- Studio launch-page composition: 1 named export. The studio location is accurate. The class offer is clear. The booking action is visible.
- Class announcement: 1 named export. The class details match the approved roster. The pictured instructor is identified accurately.
- Studio booking story: 1 named export. The booking action is inside the safe area. The studio identity is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

brand_identity.sector: Boutique reformer pilates studio
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, first studio run for four years; opening a second location on Calloway Row in a North American city. Owner led by Marit and Dana, with six instructors. Small, independent, growing to two rooms.
brand_identity.about: Verda is a boutique reformer pilates studio built on calm. One body, one room, generous air, and unhurried attention. Marit and Dana have run a single studio for four years and are now opening a second on Calloway Row. The studio is deliberately the opposite of a chain gym: no crowding, no shouting, no gloss of the everyday. What clients pay for is space, focus and a considered environment they return to.
brand_identity.audience: Considered buyers, mostly women in professional work, aged 28 to 48. They typically audition three studios before committing to one, and they are paying for calm, attention and space rather than volume or intensity.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium neighborhood, not luxury. Intro pack 180 dollars, membership 220 a month. Positioned above a high volume budget gym and below wellness luxury: the tone is soft daylight and quiet confidence, never pretension and never a discount.
brand_identity.typography: Quiet and editorial. A light, humanist serif for headlines paired with a restrained sans for body and labels. Generous spacing, small type, nothing condensed, bold or promotional.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and unhurried. Speaks to one person rather than a crowd. Confident without hype, and honest about what the room actually is.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand guidelines were ever written. The wordmark was drawn by a designer who has since left, and the only surviving file is a small low resolution web export she handed over. There is no master artwork, no color specification and no font list on record, so the freelancer inherits the studio look from this brief and from the room itself.
brand_identity.values: Calm, attention, generous space, and honesty about the room a client will actually walk into.

task_name: Cape Marren - Shoulder-season tourism campaign
client_brief:
Coastal destination imagery for the quieter season

Cape Marren's campaign runs October to April. We need a welcoming coastal image set, but not sunshine or sea conditions that misrepresent that season. Six members have contributed photographs; suitable licensed coastal imagery can fill the declared context role.

Final handoff

 Shoulder-season destination poster: 1 named export. Cape Marren is identified. Stock coastal imagery is not labelled as a named member venue.

 Destination itinerary carousel: 6 named exports. Stops use the approved member names. The sequence supports a plausible visitor itinerary.

 Tourism member feature: 1 named export. The featured member is identified accurately. The imagery corresponds to that member or is explicitly illustrative.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Regional destination marketing, an alliance of independent coastal member businesses
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A visitor alliance of twenty two independent member businesses along the Cape Marren coast on the North American Atlantic seaboard. Coordinated by Nell on behalf of the members. Small, member funded, regional in reach.
brand_identity.about: Cape Marren Coast Alliance markets a stretch of independent coast to shoulder season visitors. Summer sells itself; the work is October to April, when a harbour seafood room, a cider barn, a point light, a bookshop, a bakery and an oyster landing either make a living or do not. The campaign has to feel like that season honestly: warm low sun, weather, wool, wet stone, a lit window at four in the afternoon, quiet compositions with one or two people. Members have to see themselves in it, because members who cannot see themselves do not renew.
brand_identity.audience: Travellers aged 30 to 60, driving from within four hours, mostly couples and pairs of friends rather than families. They spend 200 to 600 dollars per party across a two or three night shoulder season weekend on rooms, meals, cider and a walk.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid range and real. Positioned above a peak summer holiday treatment (which would oversell blue water and hard sun) and below a 1,500 dollar luxury coastal weekend (which would go near monochrome and strand the bakery and the cider barn). Editorial rather than promotional, and never promising a season the coast cannot deliver in November.
brand_identity.typography: Editorial, not promotional. A quiet serif for headlines with a plain sans for captions, trail numbers and opening months. Restrained weights, comfortable spacing, nothing that reads as a sale.
brand_identity.voice: Grounded and truthful. Warm about the place without overselling it, and specific about what a visitor will actually find when they arrive out of season.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No written brand guidelines exist. The only brand file on hand is the alliance mark left by the previous agency, supplied as a single vector file with nothing else: no color system, no type list and no usage notes. Members submit their own photographs and object shots, and the campaign look is set by this brief rather than by any existing kit.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about the season, keeping every member visible, and supporting the independent businesses that fund the alliance.

task_name: Palewell Health - Licensed care image campaign
client_brief:
A restrained healthcare image set with a reliable clinical-lead cutout

Palewell needs photography that feels credible together, even though most of the set will be licensed and only one frame is owned. Please prioritise compatible camera scale, neutral balance and depth over a collection of individually attractive stock photographs.

Scope
1. Care-service information poster: 1 named export. The service wording stays within approved claims. The care contact is readable.
2. Care website header: 1 named export. Stock people are not identified as named clinicians. The service name is clear. The clinical lead has a clean hair edge on the deep brand ground.
3. Clinical lead transparent portrait: 1 named export. The portrait preserves the person in palewell_lead_frame.jpg. The shoulder edge has no visible halo.
4. Referral information panel: 1 named export. The referral steps follow approved copy. The clinical lead identity is accurate.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Care that meets you at home
brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer digital health platform with a growing employer benefits channel, sold to members and to the benefits leads who choose on their behalf
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Portland, Oregon; an eleven person team, clinician led, still owner run
brand_identity.about: Palewell is a subscription digital health platform for people managing ordinary, everyday conditions from home. Members pay a modest monthly fee for clinician backed guidance, and about half our growth now comes through employer benefits teams who offer us to their staff. We exist so that steady, unglamorous care feels reachable rather than clinical.
brand_identity.audience: Members aged thirty to fifty five who want reassurance without a hospital, plus benefits and HR leads who evaluate us for risk and coverage before putting us in front of their people
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fifteen to forty dollars a month, plus employer plans. Mid market and accessible: above a free wellness app, well below concierge medicine. The read must never feel like a two hundred dollar boutique practice or a supplement funnel.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif for headlines that reads as considered and trustworthy, paired with a clean humanist sans for body and interface. Generous air, restrained scale, nothing shouting. The type should feel like a careful letter, not a brochure.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and unhurried; we speak to a person, not a patient. We avoid hype, superlatives and clinical jargon. Example line the brand would write: "Manage the everyday stuff with someone in your corner, from home."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no formal brand book. What exists is an internal notes file describing the palette in words (a deep slate, a warm chalk, a single muted signal colour), the tone of voice, and what the founders mean by calm. We have never run a photo shoot: every image on the current site came free with the template, and we own exactly one photograph outright, of our clinical lead, cleared for use.
brand_identity.values: Credibility and warmth held together: real people in real rooms, honest about what we are, calm enough that a benefits lead trusts us with their staff.

task_name: Cordwain Overland - Identity master graphics
client_brief:
Recover three apparel graphics and prove they survive small reproduction

Cordwain has lost the working artwork for three overland graphics. We need a vector specialist who can recover what is actually in the references and make a useful garment-ready family, not deliver an unchecked automatic trace.

What we need back
- Recovered garment mark: 3 named exports. The geometry follows the authoritative source mark. The lettering is faithful to the source.
- Garment graphics application sheet: 1 named export. Placement scale matches the supplied garment constraints. The specified ink count is respected.
- Garment lookbook layout: 1 named export. The garment and graphic relationship is visible. The identity is consistent with the recovered masters.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Made for the long way round
brand_identity.sector: Mid tier overland and hiking apparel label selling graphic tees and hoodies through its own store and four independent outfitters
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016 in Bend, Oregon; a small independent label, a handful of people, direct to consumer plus four stockists
brand_identity.about: Cordwain Overland makes graphic apparel for people who drive the back roads and walk the ridgelines. Our graphics are the reason people buy: customers zoom in on the print detail before they add to cart. Every drop is a small set of designs printed with care on garments meant to be worn hard.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged twenty four to forty who care how a print is made, can tell a discharge print from a thick plastisol slab, and screenshot the print detail before they buy
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tees at thirty four dollars, hoodies at seventy eight. Mid tier: a clear step above a bargain blank, priced on print quality rather than logo. Two or three tight inks with a bit of texture read as the craft they pay for.
brand_identity.typography: A sturdy condensed sans for badge and display work, paired with a plain workhorse sans for spec sheets and store copy. Type inside the graphics is treated as drawn lettering, outlined to print. The feel is field manual, not fashion label.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plainspoken and a little dry; we talk about how a thing is made, not how it will change your life. Example line the brand would write: "Three tight inks, printed to last the season."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The brand sheet is two pages of internal notes: the palette in words, the placement rules we have always used, our maximum print widths for chest and full back, and a paragraph on what we mean by a tight print. Our old designer worked off site and we never got the layered files; for three of our best selling graphics all that survives is a few flat web exports and two printed samples we photographed on the bench.
brand_identity.values: The print is the product. We would rather run two or three honest inks with real texture than a muddy multi colour job, and we never price the line out of its own customers.

task_name: Redecker Machine Works - Restored mark system
client_brief:
Restore a machineworks identity from a catalogue and an etched plate

Redecker's mark has a long history, but the source artwork has not survived. We have a 1974 catalogue and an etched plate to work from. We want the identity recovered carefully, not replaced with something that merely looks industrial.

The commission

 Engineering identity master: 1 named export. The mark preserves the surviving original identity. Letter counters remain open at the specified reproduction size.

 Machine identity plate: 1 named export. The plate information matches the supplied machine record. The production lettering is legible.

 Service document header: 1 named export. The company name is correct. The header leaves usable space for service content.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Manufacturer of press brakes and metal forming presses, capital equipment sold to procurement engineers and plant managers across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1919 in Sheboygan, Wisconsin; third generation family works, forty one people
brand_identity.about: Redecker builds press brakes and metal forming presses, from forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars a machine. The works has carried the same company mark since 1919. Our buyer reads the tolerance sheet before he reads anything we wrote, so everything we put a name on has to say precision.
brand_identity.audience: Procurement engineers and plant managers who buy on specification rather than feeling, across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.price_positioning: Capital equipment at forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars per machine. The mark is read as evidence about the machine: the register is flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced, never heritage craft workshop and never consumer tech.
brand_identity.typography: A flat, mechanical grotesque for the mark and plate wording, set high contrast and widely spaced, paired with a plain industrial sans for the usage sheet and stationery. Nothing decorative, nothing hand drawn. Weight and spacing do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, factual and confident; we state the specification and let it stand. No adjectives a tolerance sheet would not carry. Example line the brand would write: "Built to a hundred years of the same standard, plate by plate."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We no longer hold usable artwork for the company mark in any form. The designer who last touched it retired in the nineties and nothing came back from his files. What survives is a flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, where the mark is printed in one deep ink on cream board, and a photograph a fitter took of the same mark etched into a stainless nameplate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. A works standards text file records the green as the paint shop mixes it, the address block and the required plate wording. Two further company marks also survive only as artefacts: the works proving stamp, held only as a die impression struck into a steel test coupon a fitter photographed, and the 1919 cast heritage device, held only as a raking light photograph of the badge cast and painted into a machine's main frame.
brand_identity.values: Precision as reputation: the mark on a two hundred thousand dollar machine has to be as true as the machine, reversed clean out of the works green, and unmistakably ours.

task_name: Apex Rally Club - Motorsport face and livery system
client_brief:
Six club badges rebuilt for pin and coin supplier review

Apex Rally Club needs six badge faces recovered from photographs for a pin and coin project. The references contain the colours and details we want to retain, but they are not reliable production drawings.

Deliverables
1. Motorsport face artwork: 6 named exports. The face design matches the named design record. The crest remains recognisable at the supplied reduction size.
2. Applied livery presentation: 1 named export. The graphics follow the vehicle panel boundaries. The livery hierarchy is readable at viewing distance.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

brand_identity.sector: Volunteer run amateur rally club producing hard enamel pins and struck challenge coins for its members and event tent table
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1987 in Vermont; a volunteer run club of two hundred and forty members holding six events a year
brand_identity.about: The Apex Rally Club is a volunteer amateur motorsport club in Vermont. Six events a year, and a merch table that pays for the timing gear. The club crest goes back to 1987 and each event badge, the hillclimb, the night stage, the ice trial, the gravel loop and the finale, was drawn over the years by members. This autumn is our first proper collectible run with a mint.
brand_identity.audience: Club members aged roughly twenty to forty five who already own the previous years and buy on continuity with the club's history, plus impulse buyers at the event tent
brand_identity.price_positioning: A two tier line: twelve dollar impulse pins across the tent table and ninety five dollar numbered coins a member inspects in the hand. The register is club rather than corporate: confident and worn in, never novelty and never distressed for effect.
brand_identity.typography: A worn slab or industrial serif for crest and badge lettering, carried as outlined vector, paired with a plain sans for the mint spec sheet, capsule insert and backing cards. The feel is club regalia with a straight face, history rather than novelty.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, understated and proud of the years behind us; we talk about continuity, not hype. Example line the brand would write: "Same crest we ran in 1987, struck to hold up to the light."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: None of the art exists in a form a mint will accept. What we have is six reference sheets, the crest and five event badges, printed at different times on different paper and photographed on a workbench under whatever light was in the garage. A member also sent a photo of the crest as it is embroidered on the club jackets. The mint requirements file gives diameters, the hard enamel colour ceiling, plating options and the rule that the coin's raised metal version must be line only.
brand_identity.values: Continuity with 1987: the ninety five dollar coin is bought on history, so the faces have to read as one club collection rather than six separate files, worn in but never sloppy.

task_name: Isla Verde - Monogram and wayfinding pictogram system
client_brief:
Resort identity recovery and a bilingual door-plate system

Isla Verde needs a specialist who is comfortable with both identity craft and production data. This is one coordinated job: recover the foil monogram, build the pictograms and make the bilingual plates fit the existing installation.

Final handoff

 Recovered Isla Verde monogram: 1 named export. The letterforms match the authoritative source. The inter-letter relationships preserve the original identity.

 Facility pictogram: 8 named exports. The symbol communicates the named facility. The symbol remains legible at 12 mm.

 Bilingual door plate: 25 named exports. The language pairing matches the schedule. The room identifier is unambiguous. The approved monogram is used.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent upscale coastal resort refreshing its corridor and garden wayfinding and its room signage.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Family owned, Gulf coast of Florida, a forty two room property with corridors, a garden path and about twenty four rooms and facilities.
brand_identity.about: Isla Verde is a family owned resort on the Gulf coast where guests come for quiet. Forty two rooms, refinished corridors and a garden that people walk slowly. The signage is being rebuilt this winter so the property reads as calmly as it feels, with the house monogram carried consistently from the door plates to the directional panels.
brand_identity.audience: Independent leisure travellers thirty to fifty five paying for calm, who notice when a place is shouting and value being able to find their way without being told loudly.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Upscale independent, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night. Signage should read at that tier: generous clear space, delicate marks, confidence rather than contrast for its own sake.
brand_identity.typography: A fine interlocking monogram set small and confidently, paired with a quiet, well spaced text face. Type kept modest and legible, never large or emphatic. Facility symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark.
brand_identity.voice: Understated, warm, precise. It gives directions without raising its voice. Example line: The spa is along the garden path, second door on the left.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No monogram source file survives. The designer moved abroad and nothing was handed back. The only decent record of the mark is a foil stamp on the cover of a brochure printed in 2019. The 2016 sign shop that cut the current door plates has since closed, though its press artwork for the plates is still on file.
brand_identity.values: A sense of quiet that guests can navigate, and a written standard so the next person who orders a sign does not invent something new.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Ridgeway Rovers - Football crest master system
client_brief:
Recover a football crest and its hand-drawn shirt lettering

Ridgeway Rovers wants its existing identity back in usable form. The crest needs to work at breast size and in one ink; the lettering comes from a set of 1990s drawings rather than a font we can buy.

Scope
1. Football club crest: 3 named exports. The club lettering matches the source. The crest details remain recognisable at shirt size.
2. Club number glyph: 10 named exports. The numeral is unambiguous at kit viewing distance. The glyph follows the founder's drawing.
3. Club letter glyph: 26 named exports. The letter follows the founder's drawing. The letter has no graph-paper artefacts.
4. Shirt and training-kit artwork sheet: 1 named export. The crest placement respects the supplied kit dimensions. The name-number hierarchy is usable on the shirt.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Grassroots amateur football club refreshing its playing kit, crest and shirt numbering through one local kit supplier.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1974, a village near Cirencester in the Cotswolds, with two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups.
brand_identity.about: Ridgeway Rovers are a village football club that has worn the same crest since 1974 and drawn their own shirt numbering since the nineties. This season brings the first new shirt since 2019. The club wants its own crest and its own hand drawn numbering back as proper artwork, so any supplier can print it and it still looks like Ridgeway.
brand_identity.audience: Players and parents at twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt, often buying a child's fourth kit in five years, who want something that looks like a proper club.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Grassroots, twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt printed by one local supplier. Numbering has to reduce to a single robust cuttable colour for heat press and flock, honest rather than pro tier.
brand_identity.typography: The crest lettering is small caps set in a ring. The numbering is the club's own hand drawn alphabet and digits, rebuilt as even, solid, cuttable geometry. A supporting text face for the spec and boards sits behind the drawn work, never over it.
brand_identity.voice: Straightforward, warm, club room plain. Example line: Same crest we have worn since 1974, cleaned up so any printer can do it justice.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No artwork survives. The former kit secretary took the crest files when he moved away, leaving only a parent's phone photo of the crest stitched on last season's home shirt. The numbering exists only as two marker on graph paper sheets, an alphabet and a digit set, drawn by a founding member in the nineties and photographed on a kitchen table. Last season's supplier back of shirt sheet is on hand as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping what is genuinely theirs, the 1974 crest and the founder's numbering, and reading as a real village club rather than a franchise or a school project.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Wharfside Folk Festival - Restored festival identity
client_brief:
Bring our painted festival wordmark into a usable anniversary kit

Wharfside Folk Festival is twenty years old. The shed-painted wordmark is part of that history, and we want to retain its character across the handbill, cloth and supporting anniversary materials.

What we need back
- Recovered festival mark: 1 named export. The source lettering is preserved.
- Festival poster: 1 named export. The billing order follows the approved lineup. The event date is readable.
- Festival handbill: 1 named export. The venue details are readable at print size. The ticket action is visible.
- Festival shirt artwork: 1 named export. The ink limits follow the supplier note. The mark remains recognisable on the garment.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent three night folk music festival producing a screen printed poster programme and act cards for its twentieth year.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
brand_identity.about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. Everything it prints comes off a two person hand screen shop that has printed the festival since the beginning, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.
brand_identity.audience: Festival goers and locals at thirty five to sixty dollar tickets, many of whom already own the last five years of posters and buy the new one as a twenty dollar framed keepsake.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Community festival pricing, tickets thirty five to sixty dollars and posters sold afterwards at twenty dollars. The slightly imperfect hand pulled screen look is the value, not a corner cut.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is the hand painted lettering that has been on the harbour shed since 2006. Supporting type sits beside that painted hand without imitating it, set for flat opaque ink and visible registration. Coarse tone screens carry the sky and water.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plainspoken, of the place. Example line: Three nights of folk on the old harbour, twenty years and counting.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as white paint on the weathered timber of the harbour shed, photographed from the quay, with no file and none ever made. The approved twentieth year illustration exists as a single flattened scan of a gouache and watercolour painting, no layers. The screen shop's own act card from last year is on file as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping the hand pulled, limited ink look that makes the posters worth framing, and staying continuous with nineteen years already hanging in local kitchens.

task_name: Coble and Vane - One-color mark system
client_brief:
Distillery mark recovery and a matching founder portrait set

This is a focused identity-production commission for Coble & Vane. We need the existing mark recovered in colour and true one-ink form, alongside three founder photographs that currently disagree because of their lighting.

The commission

 One-colour packaging identity: 1 named export. The mark uses the approved one-ink treatment. The counter spaces remain open on the stated stock.

 Cask-release label artwork: 13 named exports. The release details match this record. The label respects the supplied packaging area.

 Packaging supplier application sheet: 1 named export. The ink treatment is unambiguous. The application scale is stated.

brand_identity.sector: A two-person coastal distillery making small-batch gin and cask-strength single malt, sold shop-direct and through independent merchants.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, on the Northumberland coast, England. A two-person distillery: Iris runs the still, her partner runs everything else.
brand_identity.about: Coble & Vane is a working distillery on a stretch of the North Sea coast, named for the flat-bottomed fishing boat that once beached below the still house. We release twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind. The bottle is meant to earn its place on a shelf and in a hand, not to shout across the shop.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 choosing a gift or a considered bottle, and the independent merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. People who read a label closely and reward restraint.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars: standard gin at 55, cask-strength single malt from 95 to 120. Upper-craft tier, sitting deliberately apart from the twelve-dollar shelf. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax rather than by loud print.
brand_identity.typography: Display in an engraved-feeling serif with real weight in the caps, set with generous letter spacing. Text in a quiet humanist sans for supplier and label copy. The type stays out of the way and lets a single ink do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, dry, unhurried. Written as instruction, not advertisement. Example line: "One ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny. If our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house mark was drawn six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad and cannot be reached. It survives only as a full-colour illustration flattened to a single PNG. There are no vector files, no one-ink versions, and no supplier guidance sheet. Every single-colour version a supplier has ever received was improvised from that one file, and no two have matched.
brand_identity.values: Restraint and honesty. One deep ink, generous clear space, and finishes that carry the value instead of the print. Say plainly what a version can and cannot do.

task_name: Halcyon Grid - Production logo family
client_brief:
Turn rough raster brand concepts into a credible SaaS identity system

Halcyon Grid is a small logistics software team. We have three AI-generated raster marks, but we do not yet have a usable identity. We need a designer to resolve the geometry, not preserve every artefact in those images.

Deliverables
1. Halcyon Grid logo variant: 3 named exports. The geometry preserves the master identity. The lettering is optically balanced.
2. Identity usage guide: 1 named export. The guide shows usable clear-space examples. The variant naming is unambiguous.
3. Team website identity application: 1 named export. The correct team names accompany their portraits. The parent and product identities have a clear hierarchy.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A seed-stage software company selling scheduling infrastructure to logistics operations teams, with a main product and two sub-products.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Denver, Colorado. Eleven people, six weeks out from their first developer conference.
brand_identity.about: Halcyon Grid builds scheduling infrastructure for logistics operations teams, sold by the seat to the engineers and operations leads who run the floor. The product is judged on reliability, and the brand is meant to say the same thing the software does: precise, plain, and built to be depended on.
brand_identity.audience: Engineering and operations leads at mid-sized logistics firms, decided by a technical evaluator rather than a brand buyer. An audience that reads fuss as sloppiness and crispness as competence.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month. Mid-market infrastructure pricing, sold on reliability and evaluation rather than on brand aspiration. The visual language reads as engineering credibility, never as marketing spend.
brand_identity.typography: Wordmark and headings in a geometric grotesque with tight, even weight and no decorative detail. Body and documentation in a clean neutral sans with strong numerals. Type is set to read as documentation, not as a campaign.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, unadorned, engineer to engineer. No hype, no gloss. Example line: "Sharp, plain, restrained. If something in our own list turns out to be a bad idea, tell us before you build it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The three marks (the main mark and two sub-product marks) were generated by the founder in an AI tool two years ago, on separate nights with different settings. Only the soft-edged raster exports survive, with no source files. They go soft as soon as anyone scales them, and the printer and the app store listing have both said they cannot use them. No production vector artwork exists.

client_brief:

Evergreen Provisions needs the six painted crest lockups prepared for its small garment capsule. The brush character matters, but the artwork must hold at the actual garment width rather than only in a large presentation.

Please prepare
- Apparel crest production artwork: 6 named exports. The crest matches the authoritative painted reference. The brush character survives the reduction.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Bend, Oregon. Two owned dispensary shops, owner-run, with a small counter-retail apparel line.
brand_identity.about: Evergreen Provisions runs two dispensary shops in Bend, built around six house strain families. Two years ago the owners paid a local sign painter to hand-paint a crest panel for each family onto the shop walls. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them, and the first apparel capsule exists to answer that question without losing the hand that made the panels.
brand_identity.audience: Craft-minded dispensary customers aged 25 to 45 who buy at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. People who pay for the painted origin, not for a logo.

Hello from Cedar Commons. We help run the farmers' market, and the apron print is the version of our mark people recognise. Could you help us get it into a form we can place cleanly, without a box around it?

brand_identity.sector: A volunteer-run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, free to the public, funded by daily stall fees.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Volunteer-run, 36 to 44 stalls, open weekends May through October.
brand_identity.about: Cedar Commons is a neighbourhood farmers market that runs on weekends in a Burlington park, free to walk into and funded entirely by the vendors who pay a daily stall fee. It has outgrown its chalkboards and its bedsheet banner. The signage exists to get families to the right lot, past the entrance and to the stall they are looking for, printed cheaply and well at a local sign shop.
brand_identity.audience: Neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who arrive on foot or park in the wrong lot, plus the vendors and volunteers who run the morning. Read from a moving car and from across a field.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A free public market funded by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, often part-donated. Everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a local sign shop. Flat inks and heavy type, never a refined tint palette that would be unreadable outdoors and would make a free market look like it is charging.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a friendly high-contrast slab or bold grotesque, weighted to be read from a car. Wayfinding and schedule copy in a plain heavy sans with one clear instruction per sign. Real weight matters more than refinement.

brand_identity.values: Community and thrift. Recover the real mark rather than replace it, keep the set to a few flat inks that print cheaply, and tell the committee what the mark can and cannot do before they pay for plates.

task_name: Static Union - Manufacturing artwork system
client_brief:
One streetwear graphic family adapted properly for four manufacturing methods

Static Union needs production-minded artwork adaptation for small goods. The same detailed drawing will not work unchanged as embroidery, enamel, a sticker and a woven label. We are looking for someone who understands those differences and can make deliberate reductions.

Scope
1. Manufacturing artwork: 4 named exports. The artwork respects the medium-specific vendor tolerance. The smallest reproduced detail remains open.
2. Supplier production guide: 1 named export. The intended medium is stated on the relevant page. The physical reproduction size is unambiguous.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Two drops a year, made to be worn out
brand_identity.sector: Independent streetwear label making garments and, from this autumn, small goods (pins, patches, stickers) for a young direct and wholesale audience.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon. An eight person independent label run out of one studio.
brand_identity.about: Static Union is a small Portland label that puts out two considered drops a year and sells them direct and through roughly forty specialist stockists. The marks came out of the founder's own hand and the early tee runs, and they have been carried on garments for two seasons. Autumn is the first move into small goods, so the same marks now have to survive being made rather than printed.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly 17 to 30 who follow small labels, shop drops rather than seasons, and buy direct or from specialist streetwear stockists. They notice when a pack does not match.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Accessible independent streetwear. Stickers at 4 dollars, pins at 14, patches at 18, wholesale to about forty stockists. Priced to be cheap enough to collect and good enough to keep, never luxury.
brand_identity.typography: Display is a heavy condensed grotesque with a workwear feel, used for the label name and drop titles. Text is a plain, legible sans for stockist copy and specs. The type stays quiet so the marks lead.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plain, a little dry, talking to its own buyers rather than advertising. A line the brand would write: "Autumn small goods. Twelve pieces, made to last, gone when they are gone."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no proper brand kit. The four marks that matter survive only as whatever files people happened to send back over three years: two came from a printer, one exists only as a photograph of a woven cap label because the file is gone, and one came out of an old tee artwork folder. They look fine on screen and have been used for two years, but there are no editable masters.
brand_identity.values: Make a small number of things properly and stand behind the drop. A pack that does not match is not a pack.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Maison Serault - Wordmark and monogram master set
client_brief:
Recover our jewellery wordmark from three disagreeing references

Maison Serault has three captures of the existing wordmark and monogram. They disagree in apparent colour and weight. We need a careful reconstruction of the identity, not an average of three photographs.

What we need back
- Maison Serault wordmark: 1 named export. The lettering preserves the authoritative source. Optical spacing is balanced at packaging size.
- Maison Serault monogram: 1 named export. The approved letter structure is preserved. The mark remains readable at its smallest application.
- Collection packaging label: 1 named export. The product naming follows the approved collection. The finish treatment respects supplier limits.
- House stationery application: 1 named export. The brand name is readable. The layout leaves practical writing space.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent European fine jewelry house making and selling pieces through its own boutique and a small number of stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: An independent European house run by its founder, selling from one boutique plus a handful of stockists.
brand_identity.about: Maison Serault is a small fine jewelry house built around its founder's own hand. Pieces are made and sold through the boutique and a few trusted stockists, and everything leaves in packaging people keep. The house is changing box suppliers, and the new supplier needs proper artwork before it will quote.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly 30 to 55 purchasing as a gift or for themselves, plus a small number of stockists. They value discretion and craft over logos.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fine jewelry from 600 to 4,000 dollars. Positioned as an independent house: hairline refinement, high contrast, a small mark on a large quiet field, never mass market and never loud.
brand_identity.typography: A high contrast serif with genuine heritage credibility carries the house name. A quiet companion sets care copy and the address block. Type must never compete with the hairline foil mark.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, assured, unhurried. A line the house would write: "Each piece is finished by hand and meant to outlive its first wearer."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The working files are gone. The wordmark survives only as one flat export from 2019 whose source files were never sent, a phone photograph of brushed brass letters on the boutique wall, and a daylight photograph of the monogram foil blocked on an old card. The three disagree about the house colour, and there is no vector master of either mark.
brand_identity.values: Discretion and permanence. A decision made about the mark now sits on packaging for the next ten years, so it has to be right.

task_name: Ironway Run Club - Numbering and club mark system
client_brief:
Rebuild our club lettering and use it in the Founders Five bib run

Ironway Run Club's lettering comes from Del's 1994 drawings. We want the ten numerals, twenty-six letters and singlet logo made usable again, followed by the Founders Five bib production.

The commission

 Ironway club mark: 1 named export. The source club identity is preserved.

 Race numeral: 10 named exports. The numeral is distinguishable from similar digits at viewing distance. The numeral follows Del's 1994 drawing.

 Club letter glyph: 26 named exports. The letter follows Del's 1994 drawing. The weight is consistent with the restored set.

 Founders Five member bib: 39 named exports. The runner number matches this member. The number is the dominant visual.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

brand_identity.sector: Volunteer run community road running club with its own spring race, printing kit and race bibs for its members.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1994 by Del in Providence, Rhode Island. A volunteer run club with roughly thirty eight members on the books.
brand_identity.about: Ironway Run Club is a volunteer community running club in Providence with about thirty eight members. Its identity is the numbering the founder drew by hand in 1994, which the members treat as the club itself, and a screen printed club mark that survives on an old singlet. Each spring the kit goes to the heat transfer shop and every member runs the club's own Founders Five race with a bib.
brand_identity.audience: Members aged roughly 22 to 68, half of whom pin a bib on in the dark before a wet April race. Volunteers, not customers.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A forty dollar per season volunteer club with no sponsor. Everything printed must be cheap at volume and survive weather: one colour throughout, nothing that adds a plate or a pass, and nothing that looks like a paid entry event.
brand_identity.typography: The founder's hand drawn numerals and alphabet are the display face and the whole brand. A plain, sturdy sans handles member names and directory copy where legibility at a marshal's distance matters more than character.
brand_identity.voice: Friendly, plain, volunteer to volunteer. A line the club would write: "Founders Five is on. Pin your bib, mind the puddles, we will see you at the line."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No digital brand files exist. The numbering survives only as a phone photograph of the founder's original ink sheet on drafting paper, and the club mark only as a photograph of it screen printed on an old singlet. Nobody knows who made the mark and there is no file of either. Last year's bib survives as the printer's returned press PDF.
brand_identity.values: The founder's hand is the club, so it is kept faithfully. Legible beats clever, and every member gets the same thing for their forty dollars.
