task_name: Marchfield Exchange - Crest and engraving geometry system
client_brief:
Restore the Exchange crest and rebuild the suite-plate workflow

Marchfield Exchange is a listed 1911 building. The crest needs recovering from brass and letterhead references; the suite plates need updating from the 2019 production PDF. We are preserving an identity and an installation, not commissioning a redesign.

Deliverables
1. Marchfield shield-and-wreath crest: 2 named exports. The shield matches the authoritative source crest. The wreath matches the authoritative source crest. The original lettering is preserved.
2. Marchfield engraving artwork: 1 named export. The original crest identity survives the production simplification. Small counters remain open at 32 mm. The thinnest engraved stroke is at least 0.50 mm at a 32 mm crest width.
3. Suite plate: 15 named exports. The tenant name fits inside the plate trim. The approved shield-and-wreath crest is used. The artwork leaves a 12 mm clear margin.
4. Entrance plaque artwork: 1 named export. The crest is 180 mm across. Artwork stays at least 15 mm from each bolt centre. The building name is correct.
5. Lobby directory artwork: 1 named export. The crest is 120 mm across. Artwork leaves a 20 mm clear margin. Tenants appear in reconciled suite order.
6. Brass reproduction proof: 1 named export. The proof shows the crest on satin brass. The stated reproduction size is accurate. The proof identifies details that fail the 0.50 mm stroke limit.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A listed 1911 commercial building, managed by a property agent, let as office suites to professional firms, with a heritage sign programme.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Building completed 1911 in Portland, Maine. Fourteen lettable suites, overseen by a managing agent and a building board.
brand_identity.about: The Marchfield Exchange is a listed 1911 commercial building let to law, architecture and accountancy firms. The building itself, its stone entrance and brass fittings, is the reason tenants take space here. Its house crest is original to 1911, and the sign programme is being rebuilt as one coherent system that respects the building's character.
brand_identity.audience: Professional firms choosing a building with a stone entrance and brass fittings, and a building board approving the spend. Tenants who read signage as a signal of how the building is kept.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A listed heritage building letting at 45 to 75 dollars per square foot. The programme is engraved brass and stone appropriate metalwork, deep margins and generous clear space. Anything that would look at home on a retail park reads as neglect at this rent.
brand_identity.typography: A heritage serif with real credibility carries the building name and the crest lockup. A quieter companion serif or restrained roman sets the directory and suite plates, so the board reads as a document rather than as signage.
brand_identity.voice: Formal, measured, understated. A line the agent would write: "The Marchfield Exchange. Established 1911. Professional suites in the heart of the city."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No drawing, plate or digital file of the crest exists, and the original architect's practice closed in 1961. The crest survives in exactly two places: engraved on the weathered brass entry plaque, photographed on the wall, and printed on a 1950s tenant letterhead, scanned. The suite plates survive only as the 2019 sign shop's single press PDF.
brand_identity.values: The building's history is the asset, so the crest is recovered rather than reinvented, and the programme is kept editable so the agent can update a tenant name without a designer.

requirements: The shield matches the authoritative source crest.
The wreath matches the authoritative source crest.
The original lettering is preserved.

deliverable_groups.name: Marchfield engraving artwork
requirements: The original crest identity survives the production simplification.
Small counters remain open at 32 mm.
The thinnest engraved stroke is at least 0.50 mm at a 32 mm crest width.

deliverable_groups.name: Suite plate
requirements: The tenant name fits inside the plate trim.
The approved shield-and-wreath crest is used.
The artwork leaves a 12 mm clear margin.

deliverable_groups.name: Entrance plaque artwork
requirements: The crest is 180 mm across.
Artwork stays at least 15 mm from each bolt centre.
The building name is correct.

deliverable_groups.name: Lobby directory artwork
requirements: The crest is 120 mm across.
Artwork leaves a 20 mm clear margin.
Tenants appear in reconciled suite order.

deliverable_groups.name: Brass reproduction proof
requirements: The proof shows the crest on satin brass.
The stated reproduction size is accurate.
The proof identifies details that fail the 0.50 mm stroke limit.

task_name: Kantyna Nova - Private dining menu and campaign system
client_brief:
Private-dining cards, menu and opening materials for Kantyna Nova

We set one table a night at Kantyna Nova: one tasting, one wine flight. The plates were photographed during service, and now the private-dining bookings, menu and opening materials need to look as considered as the room.

Please prepare
- Tasting and wine menu: 1 named export. The fourteen approved courses appear in order on page 1. The forty-two wine entries are present on page 2. The wine grouping supports the pour sequence.
- Private-dining partner deck: 1 named export. The deck explains the private-dining offer. The price build-up follows approved copy.
- Reservations information sheet: 1 named export. The reservation wording is reproduced accurately.
- Opening feed post: 1 named export. Kantyna Nova is visibly identified. The approved booking action is readable.
- Opening story: 1 named export. The booking action remains in the safe area. The restaurant name is legible.
- Opening announcement banner: 1 named export. The opening information is accurate. The food remains the focal point.
- Guest pairing card: 14 named exports. The photograph shows the guest's assigned course. The complete wine designation fits at trim.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: One seating. One menu. One evening.
brand_identity.sector: An eighteen seat chef's tasting room with a private dining side, one seating a night, in Portland, Maine.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opening November 2026, Portland, Maine. A two person house: Marta runs the room, the chef cooks, and there will not be a third.
brand_identity.about: Kantyna Nova is a single table set once a night: one tasting, one wine flight, cooked and served by the two people who built it. The room is dark and quiet by design, so the plate is the only thing lit. Nothing is rushed, nothing is upsold, and the evening is the point rather than the meal.
brand_identity.audience: Guests thirty to fifty five who book the room as their occasion, not their dinner. They value intention over abundance and read a dark, spare room as confidence rather than as coldness.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the wine pairing. Held back and expensive without raising its voice: above a neighbourhood bistro, deliberately short of a destination tasting palace an eighteen seat opening cannot fill. Price is never a feature.
brand_identity.typography: A transitional display serif for course titles and the room's name, quiet and old world, set large but never loud. A humanist text face beneath it for descriptions, hours and prices, prices sitting at body size in the same text face with no rule, box or currency flourish.
brand_identity.voice: First person plural, plain and understated, never salesy. Example line the brand would write: 'One seating a night. Sit down and let the evening happen.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No formal brand kit exists yet. The course titles and the approved copy are set, there is a single handheld photograph of the finished room, and the owners photographed every plate themselves in the room during service. The private dining printer holds the pairing card press file. The identity is being set now for the first time.
brand_identity.values: Two makers, one honest evening. Restraint as generosity, and food worth looking at.

task_name: Corner and Cure - Cold-case label system
client_brief:
Cold-case labels and ordering tiles from our cafe's existing materials

Our sign is painted on a board screwed to the wall. Most of the food photographs were taken on a phone over the counter. Corner & Cure needs someone who can work carefully with those materials and turn them into a practical, consistent set.

Final handoff

 Cold-case label: 39 named exports. The allergen wording agrees with the approved item record. The item name is readable at label size.

 Marketplace item tile: 38 named exports. The photograph shows the named item. The restaurant identity does not obscure the dish.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Sandwiches worth leaving the block for.
brand_identity.sector: A fast casual neighbourhood deli counter with a cold case and a marketplace storefront, on a corner in Brooklyn, New York.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Brooklyn, New York; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Corner & Cure is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Brooklyn, New York, and this commission covers phase 2: counter refit, cold-case labels and signage.
brand_identity.audience: Walk up trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, deciding in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. They want appetite and honesty, not polish.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl. Impulse priced but not cheap: the price is the offer and sits large and proud, while the whole shop works to look like a place that is worth it rather than a bargain or a franchise.
brand_identity.typography: The hand painted board sign carries the name and sets the tone. Around it, a bold condensed display face for the wall board, prices and specials, prices at tile size so they read across the room, with a plain workhorse sans for hours, loyalty rules and small print. Warm and loud, never a novelty pile.
brand_identity.voice: Plainspoken, neighbourhood, a little brash and generous. Example line the brand would write: 'Pulled together, piled high, see you at the counter.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no digital version of the sign: the name survives only as a board hand painted by a sign painter twenty years ago and screwed to the wall over the slicer. Everything else was shot on the owner's phone over the counter. A two page written note holds the voice, hours, loyalty rules and section names, and the label printer holds a press file.
brand_identity.values: A family corner shop, second generation. Real food for regulars, made with the hand of a place, not a chain.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Lumora Laboratories - Retail launch and paid social system
client_brief:
Six-product retail launch: one image standard across store and paid social

Lumora Laboratories is preparing six products for specialty retail and a rebuilt store page. The photographs currently do not read as one line. We need the image foundations corrected and carried into editable launch material.

Scope
1. Retail product-page module: 6 named exports. The pack matches the named SKU. The approved benefit is readable.
2. Retail launch carousel: 6 named exports. The sequence differentiates the products. The brand appears on the opening page.
3. Paid social creative: 3 named exports. The approved product claim is unchanged. The shopping action is clear.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Clinical dermo-cosmetic actives, direct to consumer plus a specialty chain counter rollout, based in Los Angeles, California.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Los Angeles, California; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Lumora Laboratories is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Los Angeles, California, and this commission covers phase 2: skincare counter launch for the parent range.
brand_identity.audience: Women twenty eight to forty five, ingredient literate, who read the INCI list before the claim and treat whitespace and evidence as signs of seriousness.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Forty six to eighty dollars per SKU. Premium but not luxurious: near monochrome grounds, evidence led hierarchy, and a price that sits quietly beside the specification. Deliberately clear of both the fourteen dollar mass aisle and the two hundred and fifty dollar luxury counter, either of which would misread the clinical claim.
brand_identity.typography: A neo-grotesque for the wordmark, product names and headings, set with real whitespace and strong hierarchy. A clear text face for INCI lines, concentrations and specification tables, where legibility of a long ingredient string matters more than character. Clinical, never spa.
brand_identity.voice: Precise and evidence first, no hyperbole. Example line the brand would write: 'Formulated around actives, at concentrations we publish.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark is approved but exists only as a flat web scale PNG of the letterforms in one deep ink on white, exported by the founders' first designer, with no vector source on hand. The six products were photographed in house on a pale sweep across two sessions. The regulatory cleared INCI lines and claims are fixed and cannot be edited, and the specialty chain has supplied its approved counter card press file.
brand_identity.values: Clinical credibility earned through disclosure. Actives and concentrations named, nothing oversold.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Northgrove - Wholesale lookbook and hang-tag system
client_brief:
A ten-look wholesale hang-tag run with properly matched product photography

Northgrove's fall capsule is heading to stockists. Our immediate need is a dependable hang-tag pack: the correct piece, its own image and the full make note on every card. The photography comes from two mornings that do not yet look like the same collection.

What we need back
- Wholesale capsule lookbook: 1 named export. Styles are identified accurately. The page sequence supports wholesale selection.
- Garment hang tag: 11 named exports. The garment facts match this style. The care wording remains readable at tag size.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Cut and sewn to outlast the season.
brand_identity.sector: Heritage workwear with cast metal hardware, wholesale to independent stockists plus direct sale, made in Burlington, Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Burlington, Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: NORTHGROVE is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Burlington, Vermont, and this commission covers phase 2: wholesale lookbook, hang tags and launch collateral.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers and wearers twenty eight to forty five who value provenance and construction over logos, and who read fabric and make before they read a brand mark.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Seventy four to one hundred twenty eight dollars per piece, mid premium wholesale and direct. Muted grounds, full frame photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make. Deliberately clear of both the twenty four dollar fast fashion grid and the price free editorial luxury a buyer cannot work from.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is a charcoal condensed lockup beside a small olive leaf glyph. A condensed grotesque display carries headers, look titles and the poster; a sturdy text face carries the season statement, fabric and make notes, and the linesheet price grid. Heritage and plain, never costume.
brand_identity.voice: Understated and maker focused, provenance before promotion. Example line the brand would write: 'Ten pieces, cut and sewn in Burlington, meant to be worn hard.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The NORTHGROVE wordmark and olive leaf glyph are set. The whole capsule was shot flat, overhead, on a mid gray backdrop across two mornings, with the cast hardware shot separately on the bench. The collaborating club has no artwork left: its crest survives only as a photograph of an old wool pennant on a wall. Last season's hang tag exists as the printer's press file, same size and stock this year.
brand_identity.values: Locally made, built to last. Provenance and construction over logos, and partnerships that stay neighbourly.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Maison Valcere - Brand story deck and campaign document
client_brief:
An appointment-season story deck with a consistent jewellery image library

Maison Valcere needs its house-story and campaign documents ready for the autumn appointment season. The bench photography spans two sittings, and it does not yet sit together as a collection.

The commission

 House-story presentation: 1 named export. The sequence communicates the house's approved story. The packaging shown matches the supplied artwork.

 House campaign poster: 1 named export. The campaign identifies Maison Valcere. The product remains recognisable.

 House campaign feed ad: 1 named export. The approved message is readable. The brand treatment reflects the stated price position.

 House campaign story: 1 named export. The action line remains inside the safe area.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent fine-jewellery house, made to order and sold by appointment, with a small stockist channel.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, in a room above a bookshop in Montreal, Quebec. Four people, one bench.
brand_identity.about: Maison Valcere is a four-person high-jewellery house working to order for marriages and milestones. Twenty two references sit in the current book, most cut and set in-house and shown by appointment above the shop. The house sells quiet, considered pieces to clients who return once a decade, not once a season.
brand_identity.audience: Clients aged 35 to 60 buying for a marriage or a milestone, plus a short list of premium stockists. Considered, appointment-led buyers who research before they visit and expect the metal, stone and carat answered without asking.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Pieces run 900 to 6,500 dollars, positioned as appointment fine jewellery well above a mall counter and just below the named international maisons. Price is shown discreetly or not at all; the room and the book carry the value.
brand_identity.typography: Purely typographic, no symbols or icons. A high-contrast neoclassical serif with hairline serifs and a grave accent carries the wordmark and display; a restrained humanist or grotesque sans sets the specifications and body at a quiet scale. Generous letterspacing on caps, plenty of held space.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, precise, never salesy. States materials and provenance and stops. Example line: "Eighteen karat white gold, set with a single old-cut stone, made to your hand."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original wordmark artwork left with the designer who set it a decade ago. The only surviving version is a photograph of an old printed swing tag, so the mark has to be recovered from that before it can be used again. No usable logo files, colour references or type spec survive; these guidelines are being reconstructed this season.
brand_identity.values: One object per canvas, honest materials, and a mark that reads as ours at every size. Restraint is the house, not decoration.

Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

brand_identity.sector: Independent designer atelier producing a small autumn winter ready-to-wear collection, sold to press and to a wholesale buyer list.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, a small atelier in Copenhagen, Denmark. A handful of people, twelve looks a season.
brand_identity.about: Nordheim Atelier is a designer-led studio in Copenhagen making a tight seasonal collection in wool, shearling and gabardine. FW26 is twelve looks, sold to press and to roughly thirty independent stores. The house builds one editorial look each season and carries it across everything a buyer and an editor see.
brand_identity.audience: Fashion press and independent-store buyers aged 30 to 55. Readers who value cloth and construction over gloss, and who judge a collection on whether the range holds together.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Garments run 600 to 2,400 dollars, positioned as couture-adjacent designer ready-to-wear. Prices live only on the linesheet where buyers expect them; the collateral never discounts or shouts, since a sale treatment would strip the perceived value in a single spread.
brand_identity.typography: One documentary-editorial system: a strong high-contrast display serif or a condensed grotesque for covers and headlines, paired with a plain workhorse sans for captions, the season note and the linesheet. Hard contrast, tight measure, nothing decorative.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, closer to an investigative magazine than a catalogue. Names the fabric and the maker and leaves the rest. Example line: "Undyed Gotland wool, cut on the straight, made in Copenhagen."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists in only one place: a single letterpress card from the first season, photographed. The original artwork is gone. The mark is a compound lockup (wordmark, a hairline rule, and ATELIER in small caps) and has to be recovered whole from that photograph. No live logo files or type spec survive.
brand_identity.values: One collection, not twelve pictures. The cloth is the argument, grayscale and printed texture serve it, and the range must read as one hand.

task_name: Harbor Crest Realty - Open-house card campaign
client_brief:
Listing photography and six agent cards for 14 Marlowe Crescent

Harbor Crest Realty needs the house to look consistent across the listing and the open-house cards. The shooter has returned the rooms as captured; wall colour and window handling now vary from room to room.

Please prepare
- Agent open-house card: 7 named exports. The agent portrait matches the record. The property details match the fact sheet. The contact line is readable.
- Open-house property presentation: 1 named export. The rooms are shown truthfully. The enquiry information is unambiguous.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Residential real estate brokerage listing family homes across a suburban county.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2011, in Rosewood, Calderon County. A nine-agent brokerage listing around forty homes a season.
brand_identity.about: Harbor Crest Realty is a nine-person residential brokerage in Rosewood, listing suburban family homes for owners and guiding first move-up buyers through them. The firm runs a steady volume of listings a year and wants one repeatable kit that makes every listing look like it came from the same firm.
brand_identity.audience: Move-up buyers aged 30 to 45 making their first step up from a starter home, scrolling listings on a phone. Also the sellers who list with the firm and the six agents who work open houses.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Homes centre on the mid-market, with 14 Marlowe Crescent at 625,000 dollars and a 2.5 percent listing side. Positioned as sophisticated but approachable, not luxury and not discount: warm, legible, honest, with real facts and real room sizes shown plainly.
brand_identity.typography: One warm, legible system that renders cleanly on a phone and on an office printer: a friendly geometric or humanist sans for headings and figures, paired with a readable text face for the facts table and body. Comfortable sizes, clear hierarchy, nothing prestige-cold or shouty.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, welcoming, benefit-led without hype. Speaks like a neighbour who knows the street. Example line: "Four bedrooms, a garden that backs onto the ravine, and an open house this Sunday."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The firm is not rebranding. A current sign and business card are already in the field and are supplied as the basis, so the new kit must match what is out there rather than replace it. The open house card artwork is held by the printer as a press PDF; there is no central brand file beyond the sign and card reference.
brand_identity.values: Consistency across every listing, honesty in the photography, and collateral the brokerage can rebuild itself for the next home. The agent relationship is the product.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Verranza Coastal Retreats - In-villa seasonal collateral
client_brief:
Twelve seasonal villa cards and a coherent three-property image set

Looking at our Verranza photographs together, you could believe they describe three different holidays. Two trips, two photographers and a batch already edited elsewhere have left the collection inconsistent.

Final handoff

 In-villa seasonal card: 13 named exports. The season dates match this record. The villa information is unambiguous. The rate conditions are readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The whole house, the whole coast.
brand_identity.sector: Boutique luxury vacation-rental collection managing whole-property villas on the southern French coast.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Liguria, Italy; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Verranza Coastal Retreats is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Liguria, Italy, and this commission covers phase 2: booking collateral and in-villa season cards.
brand_identity.audience: Guests aged 40 to 65 booking a whole villa for a birthday, an anniversary or a multi-generation gathering, plus the travel agencies and private clients who book on their behalf. They have stayed in the real houses and will recognise anything that is not true.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Villas run 1,800 to 4,200 dollars a night depending on season, positioned against boutique hotels rather than other rentals. The grammar is generous space and quiet architecture, with rates carried in a discreet table rather than announced, so the collection never reads as an aggregator listing.
brand_identity.typography: One quiet prestige system: an elegant high-contrast serif for display and villa names, set with air, paired with a clean humanist sans for amenity tables, the rate ladder and body. Restraint over flourish, so it reads considered without tipping into fashion-house coldness a family will not book from.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, warm, understated. Describes what the house actually is at that hour, never oversells. Example line: "Warm stone, a long terrace, and the pool in real afternoon light."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The collection has a printed in-villa season card whose artwork is held by its printer as a press PDF, and a written owner note recording what the previous editor got wrong. There is no lost wordmark here; the constraint is photographic consistency across three villas shot on two trips by two people, with the second batch already worked on by an editor no longer used. The collection's one graphic mark is a small hand inked cove motif an artist drew for the founders, which survives only as a flatbed scan of the original inking and as the mark etched on Maison Aubine's door glass; it has never been redrawn or digitised, and the foil printer and the glass etcher need it as vector artwork. The contractual welcome provision left in every house exists only as a short still life set the manager shot on a villa's limestone counter.
brand_identity.values: Believable before impressive. One collection, not three holidays. Natural light, real shadow, honest water, and no fake high dynamic range or dyed pools.

Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Nimbadesk - B2B sell-sheet system
client_brief:
Nimbadesk launch collateral using the current product build

We need the sell sheets, pitch deck and launch social to look like one product. There are eleven product captures in the pack, but the first job is to establish which belong to the current build and how they should be presented consistently.

Scope
1. B2B product sell sheet: 4 named exports. The stated metric preserves its qualification. The UI is a faithful supplied capture.
2. Product pitch deck: 1 named export. The narrative explains the customer problem before the offer. The claims follow approved copy.
3. Product launch post: 3 named exports. The product name is clear. The request-demo action is visible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: B2B help desk software sold per seat to IT and operations leads at fifty to five hundred person firms.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Denver, Colorado, an eleven person team fourteen months into private beta.
brand_identity.about: Nimbadesk is help desk software for the internal IT and operations teams that keep mid sized companies running. We replace the tangle of shared inboxes and half configured legacy tools with one queue, clear ownership and reporting a director can actually read. We sell to the person who has to defend the line item, so everything we show is real: real screens, real numbers, real periods.
brand_identity.audience: IT and operations leads aged thirty to fifty at fifty to five hundred person firms who sign annual contracts and route the invoice past a finance director. They evaluate carefully, compare tiers before reading copy, and distrust hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Per seat tiers at 29, 79 and 249 dollars, with enterprise annual near 18,000. Mid market: above the free consumer tools, well below the enterprise suites, priced to be defended rather than impulse bought.
brand_identity.typography: A calm geometric sans for display, set tight at a real hierarchy, paired with a highly legible neutral sans for body and a tabular numeric face for metrics and the tier table. The feel is engineered and quiet, never showy.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, specific, understated. Numbers carry the argument and every claim states its period. Example line the brand would write: "Thirty one teams moved their queue to Nimbadesk this year. Here is what changed, and over what window."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No source files exist. The mark was generated by our first designer with an AI tool and delivered only as a flat picture, which is the single copy anywhere. There is no vector, no guideline document and no defined weight. Screenshots were captured ad hoc across the year at whatever scale the display was set to.
brand_identity.values: Evidence over theatre, and software a finance director would sign off without flinching.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Alderwood Scholars Fund - Multi-center appeal campaign
client_brief:
Five-centre appeal banners with accurate local details and a recovered crest

Alderwood Scholars Fund needs one coordinated banner run for its five centres. The office must be able to trust each centre's name, address, hours and coordinator, not proofread five designs assembled independently from memory.

What we need back
- Centre appeal banner: 5 named exports. The beneficiary story matches the named centre. The programme amount agrees with the reconciled funding table. The donation action is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An education charity running five after school learning centres and a small scholarship fund across greater Providence.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, greater Providence, Rhode Island, four staff, a volunteer board and five centres.
brand_identity.about: Alderwood Scholars Fund runs five after school learning centres and a scholarship fund for students across greater Providence. This winter marks our twentieth year. The year end appeal carries roughly half our giving, and it works because donors trust that the money reaches the students rather than the overhead. We show our numbers plainly, name where every dollar went, and let the work speak.
brand_identity.audience: Mission motivated donors aged forty five to seventy who give because they believe in the work. Several read the overhead ratio before the narrative and reward organisations that look like they spend on students, not on production.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Average gift 45 dollars, major asks 5,000 to 50,000. Community scale and grassroots: careful and credible rather than glossy, every visible dollar of production reading as an in house afternoon rather than an agency retainer.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif for headlines and the twentieth year milestone, with a plain humanist sans for body, captions and tables. Numbers set in a clear tabular figure so charts and the spend breakdown read honestly. The feel is settled and civic, not corporate.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, quietly proud. It credits students and staff, states periods on every figure, and never begs. Example line the brand would write: "Last year, ninety students finished the programme. Here is where your gift went, line by line."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The crest was drawn by a trustee in 2006 and the artwork files are long gone. The only surviving version is the enamel crest on the front wall of the Eastgate centre, which we have as a single handheld photograph. There is no vector, no guideline sheet and no recorded palette or type.
brand_identity.values: Money goes to students, and the books reconcile in public.

task_name: Lanternwood Folk Fest - Performer credential system
client_brief:
Performer laminates for Lanternwood, rebuilt from last year's printed artwork

Twenty-two people need correct performer laminates. Our designer left in 2024, and the usable starting point is last year's printed artwork. We need a production designer who will rebuild the run carefully, not carry last year's names or fields into new passes.

The commission

 Performer credential: 23 named exports. The access category matches the performer record. The portrait belongs to the named performer. The credential remains readable when worn.

brand_identity.tagline: Three stages, one field, after dark.
brand_identity.sector: An independent three stage folk and roots music festival held on a farm outside Burlington, sixth edition.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: outside Burlington, Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Lanternwood Folk Fest is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is outside Burlington, Vermont, and this commission covers phase 1: performer passes and on-sale campaign.
brand_identity.audience: A discovery led crowd aged eighteen to forty, scene literate rather than corporate, who buy on atmosphere and word of mouth and expect the field weekend to feel real rather than packaged.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Weekend general admission 145 dollars, VIP 320, roughly four thousand weekend tickets. Mid tier independent: energetic and coherent, a credible VIP tier without tipping into either luxury restraint or bargain flyer chaos.
brand_identity.typography: A bold condensed display face for the lineup and the headline nights, carrying a real hierarchy that separates headline from discovery at a glance, paired with a sturdy grotesque for body, set times and the site plan legend. The feel is poster energy, warm and a little rough, never polished.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, a bit of grit. It talks up the discovery stages as loudly as the headliners and keeps sponsor and billing lines exactly as agreed. Example line the brand would write: "Gates at five. Three stages till late. Come early for the names you will be bragging about next year."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our designer left in 2024 and took the logo files. The mark now survives only as a photograph of the painted canvas banner that has hung over the main stage since 2022. There is no vector, no source file and no written type or colour spec. Last year's photography was shot by two volunteers on two cameras with no brief.
brand_identity.values: Give the discovery acts the poster space, and keep the weekend feeling like a field rather than a brand.

task_name: Umbra Loft - After Dark event campaign
client_brief:
After Dark: a coherent poster and social campaign from six different nights

Umbra Loft's autumn programme needs to feel like a series, even though our six usable archive photographs were shot under six different lighting rigs. We want a strong two-colour and grain treatment that actually lives in the images, not a collection of unrelated pictures behind matching text.

Deliverables
1. After Dark poster direction: 3 named exports. The billing order follows the supplied list. The event information is readable.
2. Promoter pitch deck: 1 named export. The three directions are meaningfully distinct. The sequence explains the series identity.
3. Night release post: 9 named exports. The date matches this event. The ticket action is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An independent two hundred and fifty capacity basement live music room programming a nine night autumn jazz and after dark series.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, a basement room under a former textile mill in Providence, Rhode Island, a small independent team.
brand_identity.about: Umbra Loft is a two hundred and fifty capacity basement room under an old mill in Providence, programming jazz and after dark nights for a crowd that finds us through friends and phones at eleven at night. This autumn we are running nine nights as one series rather than nine separate shows. It has to look like one thing, and it has to look like the room it actually is: dark, close and made by hand.
brand_identity.audience: A scene literate, discovery driven crowd aged twenty one to thirty five, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night, who read polish as inauthentic and reward work that plainly comes from the room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tickets 18 to 32 dollars, capacity 250. Independent basement scale: deliberately made and high contrast, credible at a headline ticket without ever reading as corporate or sponsored programming.
brand_identity.typography: A raw, weighty display face for act names and dates, set large and blunt, paired with a plain condensed grotesque for billing, door times and the room data tables. Two colours do the work over a deep ground, with grain that reads as film. The feel is gig poster made deliberately, not clip art chaos.
brand_identity.voice: Terse, atmospheric, unvarnished. It names the act, the night and the door and gets out of the way. Example line the brand would write: "Doors 8. Downstairs. Two sets, one room, cash on the night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We build the look from our own archive, six photographs shot on six nights under six touring rigs, no two matching. Three headline acts sent their wordmarks only as photographs of tour shirts and a tote, which their managers say is all that survives. There is no defined palette, type or treatment yet, and last season's printed card exists only as the press PDF our printer returned.
brand_identity.values: Everything comes from this room, on these nights, and it should never look like a bank's jazz sponsorship.

task_name: Marisol Cove - Shoulder-season hospitality campaign
client_brief:
Shoulder-season hospitality campaign built from carefully matched photography

Marisol Cove needs a shoulder-season campaign that reflects the light we actually have. Most of the coastal pictures will be licensed; the usable room photographs are ours. The work is to make them belong together, not to promise a different coast or a different property.

Please prepare
- Shoulder-season key visual: 1 named export. The pictured property is correctly identified. The offer preserves its conditions.
- Hospitality booking story: 1 named export. The booking action stays inside the safe area.
- Seasonal offer card: 10 named exports. The rate period is clear. The property identity is visible.
- Seasonal hospitality brochure: 1 named export. The offer is understandable without the original brief. The property imagery is truthful.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The quiet side of the coast.
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen room boutique hotel on the bluff above a cove, selling nights and the dining room to couples and small groups.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, on the Mendocino coast of Northern California, run by two owners with nine staff.
brand_identity.about: Marisol Cove is a small clifftop hotel built around a path down to a private beach and a dining room people plan a trip for. There is no pool and no spa, and the point of the place is the light, the water and being left alone. The autumn and winter shoulder season is the first the owners are pushing properly.
brand_identity.audience: Couples and small groups aged 30 to 55, experience led rather than amenity led, who book for the setting and the food and return in the quiet months.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Rooms run 340 to 620 dollars a night. Boutique premium, above a coastal inn and well below a resort or private estate. The rate is carried by the setting, not by facilities.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high contrast serif for display, set large and given air, paired with a plain humanist sans for rates, captions and body. Coastal premium, never resort brochure and never luxury estate. Generous leading, restrained sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, plain and specific. It describes what is actually there and lets the reader picture it. Example line the brand would write: An hour before sunset the light comes off the water and the whole cove goes gold. That is when to walk down.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The logo file was lost with the designer who drew it in 2019. The mark, a small caps wordmark over a hairline wave rule, survives only as the painted sign at the entrance, which the owners have photographed. Room photography is the owners' own phone frames plus licensed stock. No usable brand files remain beyond the sign photo.
brand_identity.values: One place under one light. Every guest facing piece should read as the same specific cove, honest about a fourteen room hotel rather than dressed up as something grander.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Lumen Quarterly - Autumn editorial issue
client_brief:
Lumen Quarterly's autumn issue, with an editable layout and recovered masthead

The editor will still be moving copy close to publication. Lumen Quarterly needs an autumn issue document that remains genuinely editable, supported by a coherent fourteen-frame photo essay and a usable version of our scanned masthead.

Final handoff

 Autumn editorial issue: 1 named export. The complete approved article is present. The image order follows the editorial sequence. The masthead preserves the approved lettering. The page hierarchy supports sustained reading.

 Editorial plate card: 15 named exports. The plate caption matches this record. The image corresponds to the named plate.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An independent arts and culture quarterly, published four times a year around one long photo essay and its writing.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Published by Lumen House Press, a two person imprint in Portland, Maine, founded 2016.
brand_identity.about: Lumen Quarterly is a print magazine about art, craft and the people who make things along the coast. Each issue turns on one photo essay and about two thousand words of reporting. Readers pay for it because it is good to hold and worth keeping on a shelf, not for news.
brand_identity.audience: Design literate readers aged 30 to 55 who buy the object as much as the article and renew a subscription because the magazine is made with care.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Eighteen dollars a single copy, sixty dollars a year. An independent object priced above a newsstand title and below an art book, sold on typographic craft rather than volume.
brand_identity.typography: The whole product is the type. A refined display serif for the masthead and openers, a readable book face for the two thousand word body at a generous measure, a quiet sans for captions, credits and folios. Real hierarchy, white space the eye rests in.
brand_identity.voice: Considered, warm and exact, written like an essay rather than a pitch. Example line the brand would write: He has built the same hull the same way for forty years, and he still stops to look at the grain before the first cut.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house style guide was made by the magazine's first designer, who has left, and it is now a couple of issues out of date on type. The masthead artwork inside the guide is a flattened screenshot, so the only proper record of the wordmark is the printed cover, which has been scanned. The printer also returned last season's press file.
brand_identity.values: Every issue should feel like the same magazine. Continuity of type, measure and picture treatment is the identity, and the reader should recognise Lumen before reading a word.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Aldervale Mutual - District insurance counter-card run
client_brief:
Rebuild our insurance counter-card template and produce the district run

The printer who made Aldervale Mutual's counter cards has closed. We still have the press file and need a reusable production route, not a one-time approximation of the design.

Scope
1. District insurance counter card: 15 named exports. The compliance wording is reproduced without alteration. The contact information belongs to this producer. The rate qualification is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Owned by the people we cover.
brand_identity.sector: A policyholder owned mutual life insurer selling whole life and final expense through appointed producers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: central Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Aldervale Mutual is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is central Vermont, and this commission covers phase 1: producer sales and compliance kit.
brand_identity.audience: Households aged 35 to 60 with modest savings, buying because they do not want to leave a burden. They trust plainness and distrust anything that reads like a sales pitch.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premiums run 45 to 180 dollars a month, drop in comparison irrelevant. A regulated mutual at a modest, accessible band, deliberately not a private wealth manager and not a discount direct response mailer.
brand_identity.typography: Type that carries authority without announcing itself. A traditional text serif for body and disclosures, a clean sans for labels and figures, one restrained accent used only to mark the recommended plan. Generous white space, tables that read like tables.
brand_identity.voice: Sober, plain and reassuring, written the way a trusted advisor speaks across a table. No exclamation, no urgency. Example line the brand would write: A whole life policy is a promise that holds its value, and the premium you start with is the premium you keep.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The printer who built the counter cards has closed, so the only counter card artwork that survives is the flat press PDF that went to press. Producer headshots are self submitted from personal phones and vary widely. Compliance owns the disclosure language and updates it when a state changes its rules.
brand_identity.values: Nothing may read as an advertisement, and everything must survive the kitchen table. Compliance and honesty come before flourish, and the material should feel as dependable as the carrier behind it.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Anvil and Oak - Gym opening member collateral
client_brief:
Athlete cards and spotlight portraits for our gym opening

Anvil & Oak needs opening-roster cards and a consistent portrait set. Sixteen members were photographed across three evenings, and the colour differences are obvious when the portraits sit on our dark ground.

What we need back
- Opening-roster athlete card: 17 named exports. The portrait belongs to the named athlete. The athlete number is clear.
- Opening gym spotlight: 3 named exports. The gym identity is visible. The opening message follows approved copy.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An independent strength and functional training studio selling coached memberships and drop in sessions.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Providence, Rhode Island; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Anvil and Oak is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Providence, Rhode Island, and this commission covers phase 1: studio opening identity and member cards.
brand_identity.audience: People aged 25 to 45 choosing coached strength work over a commodity gym, here to get strong, who value programming detail and competence over amenities.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Memberships run 110 to 185 dollars a month with a 28 dollar drop in. Roughly double a chain gym, priced on coaching. Confident and specific, neither a soft boutique wellness studio nor a discount chain.
brand_identity.typography: Heavy condensed display type for headlines and the schedule grid, held in check by a plain workhorse sans for body, times and figures. Legible from across a room, comfortable at small sizes. Confident, unsoftened, industrial without being a novelty.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plain and sure of itself, the way a good coach cues a lift. No hype, no percentages shouted. Example line the brand would write: Show up, do the work, add weight. We handle the programming so you can focus on the bar.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no logo file. The mark, an anvil silhouette inside a ring of lettering with an oak sprig crossing the anvil's horn, exists only as the sign painter's hand painted work on the studio's brick wall, which the coaches have photographed. Athlete portraits were shot by the coaches over three evenings and are not consistent. The old printer's press file is all that survives of the athlete card.
brand_identity.values: One mark, everywhere, complete and on the dark ground. The identity is the recovered wall mark used consistently, and the studio should always read as coached strength at its true price.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Apexguard - Product label and dealer collateral system
client_brief:
Dealer-ready roll labels and bay imagery for Apexguard

Our dealer meetings need a reliable label system, not another set of labels assembled one by one. Apexguard has three tiers that should read as one family, and the current stock export must control the product information.

The commission

 Product roll label: 13 named exports. The tier is identified accurately. The required installation copy fits at label size.

 Dealer range brochure: 1 named export. The product tiers are easy to compare. The uses are supported by the approved range data.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating supplied to dealer groups and to independent installers who buy film by the roll.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Charlotte, North Carolina; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Apexguard Surface Systems is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Charlotte, North Carolina, and this commission covers phase 2: dealer labels and channel collateral.
brand_identity.audience: Dealer group principals and fixed operations managers aged 35 to 55 deciding whether to put us on their reconditioning line, and independent installer owners aged 28 to 50 who buy film by the roll and post their own work. Behind both sits a vehicle owner aged 30 to 55 protecting a sixty thousand dollar car.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Full PPF installs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars, tint packages 400 to 1,200 dollars, film by the roll to installers 900 to 4,200 dollars. Premium performance tier, well above discount tint shops and deliberately not tuner.
brand_identity.typography: A single near technical system: a tight modern grotesque for the mark, headings and tier names set in confident spacing, paired with a clean humanist sans for spec tables and body so performance numbers read as data. No display flourish, no italic drama.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, exact, performance led. States numbers and lets them carry. Example line the brand would write: Ten year warranty, self healing topcoat, 92 percent clarity retained. No exclamation points, no percentage flashes, no hype.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The rebrand mark was drafted for us by an earlier round and no working file survives. What we hold is a flat raster export of the drafted master mark and a phone photograph of the installer shop card that was printed from an earlier revision of it. The mark has to be recovered as real artwork before the rollout can carry it, and the three tier marks brought alongside so the family reads as one.
brand_identity.values: Performance stated honestly and warranted as written. One brand across every surface, from the top of a dealer deck to the end of a film box.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

1600 px transparent raster companion for placement and preview.
White vector variant for approved dark-ground use.

task_name: Kilnmore - Wholesale relaunch campaign
client_brief:
Kilnmore wholesale relaunch: preserve the glazes across the full campaign

The relaunch needs to look like one Kilnmore range. We have fourteen captures from two very different mornings, covering thirteen pieces, and four glazes that customers must still be able to distinguish after correction.

Deliverables
1. Wholesale relaunch deck: 1 named export. The range story supports a trade buying conversation. The product facts are accurate.
2. Wholesale paid-social creative: 2 named exports. The trade enquiry action is visible.
3. Storefront range banner: 1 named export. Kilnmore is identified. The range remains recognisable.
4. Product specification tile: 13 named exports. The item geometry matches this record.
5. Wholesale range one-pager: 1 named export. The product hierarchy is clear.
6. Mark and type reference: 1 named export. The typography choices are identified accurately.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A small matte glaze ceramics studio selling direct through its own online storefront and wholesale to independent home goods stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Portland, Maine; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Kilnmore is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Portland, Maine, and this commission covers phase 2: wholesale line sheets and storefront launch.
brand_identity.audience: Direct buyers aged 28 to 50 who own two or three considered kitchen objects and are choosing between us and a comparable studio line, and independent home goods stockists whose buyers judge a range on whether the line sheet is legible and complete enough to order from.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mugs 34 dollars, bowls 42 dollars, serving platter 96 dollars, four piece dinner set 180 dollars. Wholesale at roughly half of retail. Considered studio ceramics, not impulse marketplace and not gallery austerity.
brand_identity.typography: One warm, legible system: a quiet humanist serif for the mark, headings and range names, paired with a clean sans for the specification tables and dimensions so a stockist reads them without effort. Warmth without decoration, nothing script, nothing ornamented.
brand_identity.voice: Plain and warm, the studio talking about its own work. Example line the brand would write: Thrown and glazed in small batches, made to be used every day. No sale language, no urgency, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark is a brush drawing inked years ago onto an unglazed clay tile, and the only version that exists is a photograph of that tile on the bench. There is no working file. The mark has to be recovered from the photograph as artwork the studio can use at any size before the relaunch can carry it. The written guideline survives, plus a phone snap of the shop counter kept as a warmth reference.
brand_identity.values: Honest materials shown plainly, and one line that reads as one line across every piece and every page.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Northwind Advisory - Team page and recruitment collateral
client_brief:
Make eight advisers look like one firm across the site and leave-behind

Northwind Advisory's team photographs were taken on three separate mornings. At present, we look like three different firms. We need a coherent portrait treatment and the team page, capabilities leave-behind and announcement posts built around it.

Please prepare
- Advisory team-page composition: 1 named export. Each portrait is paired with the correct adviser. Professional credentials match the supplied record.
- Capabilities leave-behind: 1 named export. The sector offer is clearly structured. No unsupported credential is added.
- Recruitment announcement: 1 named export. The approved role or recruitment offer is clear. The application action is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Boutique institutional wealth advisory serving endowments, foundations and around forty families.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2009, Boston, Massachusetts, eight advisers on one floor on Federal Street.
brand_identity.about: Northwind Advisory Partners advises endowments, foundations and around forty families on the long term stewardship of institutional and family capital. We are eight people on one floor, and most mandates we win begin with a trustee reading our team page and deciding whether we look like a firm they can place a hundred million dollars with. The brand exists to signal exactly that: a fiduciary, uniform, unshowy, credentialled, judged by a committee rather than an audience.
brand_identity.audience: Endowment trustees, foundation investment committees and families with twenty million dollars and up. Readers aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages and reviewing a credentials table before a mandate is placed.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Billed 350 to 600 dollars an hour. Boutique institutional tier: understated and fiduciary, deliberately not luxury editorial personal branding and not startup about us.
brand_identity.typography: One classical system: a restrained transitional serif for the firm name, headings and the credentials table, paired with a quiet sans for labels and contact lines. Wide margins, generous leading, a text size a trustee reads without effort. No display face, no oversized first names.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, plain, institutional. Speaks of stewardship and process, never of performance promises. Example line the firm would write: We advise a small number of institutions and families on capital they intend to hold for generations. No superlatives, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The firm mark is a compass rose and wordmark. Two versions survive and neither is a working file: a flat raster export pulled off the old website, and a photograph of the letterpressed card the mark was originally cut for. The mark has to be recovered as placeable artwork with its counters intact before the rebuilt pages can carry it. A third rendering survives on a foil-blocked presentation folder that carries the compass rose alone at large scale, and the only standalone emblem the old web developer ever produced is a fuzzy favicon that blurs at any size, so the mark cannot ship as one lockup: it has to be rebuilt as a working family across formats, from letterhead down to the browser icon, with its counters holding at every reproduction size. Regulated credential designations must be reproduced exactly as the practice system holds them.
brand_identity.values: Fiduciary stewardship above all, and a uniform, sober face that reads as one firm rather than eight individuals.
