task_name: Walter Fernwood Memorial - Service print and remembrance set
client_brief:
Memorial print and a memory book for Walter Fernwood's family

My father, Walter Fernwood, died in March. We are preparing the service and would like the printed pieces to sit alongside those from my mother's service in 2019. We have the old press files, a eulogy and a shoebox of scans spanning many years.

Final handoff

 Memorial keepsake card: 27 named exports. The memorial name is correct. The wording remains respectful.

 Framed memorial page: 1 named export. The dates agree with the family record. The portrait identity is preserved.

 Family memory book: 1 named export. The chronology follows the family notes. The eulogy is not rewritten. The images preserve documentary identity.

 Memorial share card: 1 named export. The memorial details are readable. The treatment is restrained.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A private heritage and memorial keepsake commissioned by a family for a service and to keep afterwards.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Commissioned 2024 by the Fernwood family, Brattleboro, Vermont, for a service of around sixty people at the Congregational hall.
brand_identity.about: This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. It is a book, not a photo album: plates with captions, a contents page, and the granddaughter's eulogy laid out in the middle, alongside a framed page and a small card for mourners to take home. The visual voice is set by two things: the family's wish that nothing be brightened or invented, and the funeral home pieces made for Walter's late wife in 2019, which the new work should sit beside on the shelf.
brand_identity.audience: The family and around sixty mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens, many of whom remember the people in the photographs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars. Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil, nor a discount photo book with grids and script headings. What the money buys is restraint.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet classical text face set large enough for a seventy year old to read without glasses, paired with a modest sans for captions and contents. Generous white space, plates given room, plain captions, one unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. No script, no decorative corners.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, gentle, unsentimental. Lets the photographs and the family's own words carry. Example line the book would write: The company toured for eleven seasons, and this is his father's hand on the back of the card. No cheerfulness, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no brand file. The look is inherited from the funeral home's two 2019 press files (a keepsake card and a framed page) that the family wants matched so the pieces sit together on the shelf, and from the family's own scans, eulogy and typed transcriptions. The funeral home's designer has retired and left only flat press files. Damage in the scans is to be shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
brand_identity.values: Nothing invented and nothing brightened. Honesty to the photographs as they are, and a keepsake the family can keep editing until the day of the service.

task_name: Harborline Realty - Weekly listing sheet system
client_brief:
Restore a weekly property-sheet workflow from our retired printer's PDF

Every Monday, Harborline Realty prints a sheet for each active listing. The printer retired with the working file. We need the process rebuilt so the current list controls the output, while the starter homes and premium properties retain appropriate, distinct image treatments.

Scope
1. Weekly property listing sheet: 12 named exports. The photograph belongs to this listing. The listing status is current in the supplied register. The agent contact is clear.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent residential brokerage selling coastal Maine homes, from corner lot starters to waterfront point estates, to local and out of state buyers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2009, harbour front office on the mid coast of Maine, eight agents under principal Dana Marlow.
brand_identity.about: Harborline is a small owner run brokerage that lists the whole mid coast book, a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter one week and a waterfront estate the next. It runs on repeat referrals and reputation in town, and prints a fresh listing sheet for every active property each Monday. Dana Marlow built it to feel like the place it sells, not a national franchise.
brand_identity.audience: Two buyers in one weekly run: estate buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility, and first time buyers under thirty five who need price, bed count and open house time to land at a glance.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One brokerage spanning a 320 thousand dollar starter to a 4.5 million dollar point estate; the sheet has to flex between the two without either register looking wrong. Weekly production retainer, roughly 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headlines and prices, an even colour that reads calm on the estate sheets. A clean humanist sans for the beds, baths and square feet strip and the agent line. Estate sheets lean on space and small type; starter sheets carry weight and size so the price reaches across a room.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grounded, mid coast. We describe the house, not ourselves, and never oversell. Example line the brand would write: 'Corner lot, three beds, a short walk to the harbour. Open Sunday, one to three.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo artwork was lost years ago. The only surviving version of the mark, a rope ring around a lighthouse with the letters H and R, is the one painted in cream on the office window. There are no brand guidelines or type specimen; the retired printer's last press file is the sole reference for the listing sheet.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about price and condition, and one consistent office look across every listing no matter who shot the photograph.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Cedarline Institute - Cohort credential system
client_brief:
Two credential registers rebuilt into a checked autumn graduation run

Cedarline Institute needs credentials for completing candidates across two registers. We have press files from two closed print shops, and they may not convert into the same kind of working document.

What we need back
- Cohort credential: 31 named exports. The credential title follows the programme code. The recipient name fits without clipping. The seal is faithful to the authoritative reference.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent continuing professional education institute running a community evening programme and an employer funded executive programme from two campus buildings.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1978, two campus buildings in Vermont, cohort run by registrar Helen Abbott.
brand_identity.about: Cedarline teaches working adults across two very different registers: an accessible community evening course and a high cost executive programme bought by employers. Each autumn cohort finishes with a ceremony where every candidate leaves with a certificate in hand and a file in their inbox the same evening. The Institute trades on being trusted rather than flashy, and on the two credentials reading honestly for what they cost.
brand_identity.audience: Community students in their twenties and thirties whose certificate is read by family at home, and executive candidates whose employer funded credential ends up framed in an office where their own clients see it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Two credentials an order of magnitude apart: a 180 dollar community certificate and a 9,000 dollar employer funded executive credential. Neither can come off the press looking like the other. Cohort run posts around 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.
brand_identity.typography: An engraved, higher contrast serif for the executive register, set with generous margins and the seal given room. A warmer, plainly legible serif for the community certificate. The two share bones but never the same weight or spacing.
brand_identity.voice: Measured and earned, never boastful. We state what was completed and who signed it. Example line the brand would write: 'Completed the autumn programme in professional practice. Signed at Cedarline Institute, Vermont.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The seal die went to the printer that closed and cannot be recovered. The only surviving seal is the one blind embossed into an old certificate, plus a raking light photograph of that impression. Two dead press files remain, last year's community certificate and the 2019 executive diploma; there is no digital seal artwork.
brand_identity.values: Each credential must be honest about its price, and every candidate name spelled and accented correctly right up to the ceremony morning.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Meridian Summit - Conference badge and wayfinding system
client_brief:
Eighteen conference badges with portraits that match and records that do not drift

The Meridian Summit registration desk needs a correct badge for every attending delegate. We have eighteen self-submitted photographs and last year's venue-bureau PDF, but not its working file.

The commission

 Conference delegate badge: 20 named exports. The access category matches the registration. The portrait belongs to the delegate. The delegate name is readable when worn.

 Conference track direction sign: 3 named exports. The track name follows the approved track note. The arrow points in the specified direction.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The people who run the grid, and the people who fund it.
brand_identity.sector: Invitation only annual executive summit for regional transmission operators, infrastructure investors and utility policy staff, produced by Meridian Council.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2016, produced from Providence, Rhode Island; one closed door summit a year, two days, eighteen seats.
brand_identity.about: Meridian Council runs a single invitation only summit each year for the small group that plans and pays for the electrical grid. It is deliberately intimate, closed door, and expensive, and everything a delegate touches at the venue is meant to feel like it cost what the seat cost. The summit works across three tracks, Operators who run the network, Capital who fund it, and Policy who regulate it.
brand_identity.audience: Eighteen delegates aged forty to sixty five who run regional transmission networks, sit on infrastructure funds or write utility policy, and have been to two hundred conferences already. For half the room the title is the reason they are in it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twenty four hundred dollars a seat, eighteen seats, invitation only. The register must read heavy, quiet and photo forward; anything bright or colour blocked reads as a name sticker at this price. Comparable commissions run 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, high contrast serif for the delegate name, set large and calm. A restrained sans in small caps for the organisation and the track distinction, carried as a typographic difference rather than a colour block. Generous space throughout, the portrait treated like a portrait.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and precise. We name who is in the room and why, and let the restraint do the talking. Example line the brand would write: 'Two days. Eighteen seats. A closed working session, not a stage.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no working file for the badge; last year's was made by the venue's print bureau from artwork nobody kept. The only clean version of the summit mark that survives is the engraving on the brass lectern plate, photographed under the room's downlights. The registration board, the two session door cards and the closing slides do not exist yet.
brand_identity.values: Names and organisations exactly as registered, nothing shortened or abbreviated, and restraint carried as the signal of credibility.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Halden and Roe - Marlow trade catalog
client_brief:
A reusable A4 trade catalogue for Halden & Roe's Marlow range

Sixteen pieces need to reach the trade show as one coherent Marlow range. Our studio photography covers two days, and the only page artwork is the flat PDF the printer made three seasons ago.

Deliverables
1. Marlow product trade sheet: 17 named exports. The photograph depicts this piece. The glaze description preserves its supplied qualification. The trade price is readable.
2. Trade catalogue cover and contents: 1 named export. The collection is identified. The contents use the item register order.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Small hand thrown stoneware house selling the Marlow range wholesale to independent homeware shops and interior stylists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2011, a small studio in Brattleboro, Vermont; everything thrown and glazed on site, sold through two reps.
brand_identity.about: Halden and Roe is a maker led stoneware house where every piece in the Marlow range is thrown and glazed by hand in the back room. It sells to buyers who order from a printed book rather than a website, one piece to a page, the way it always has. The glazes are the whole product, so the book has to let a reactive oatmeal, a gloss celadon and a matte slate tell themselves apart.
brand_identity.audience: Independent homeware shop owners and interior stylists aged thirty to fifty five, who buy around forty lines a season across a dozen makers and can tell a thrown piece from a cast one across a room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Trade 38 to 410 dollars a piece, retailing 100 to 900. The book must read airy and slow, the glaze given room to be the subject and the trade price stated plainly and once; any tight grid or shouted price collapses the margin the house runs on. Comparable work runs 2,000 to 4,000 dollars fixed.
brand_identity.typography: A small, calm serif set with real space around it, one piece to a page. Captions and the eight row spec block set quietly in deep neutrals; the trade price stated once, plainly, never boxed or starred.
brand_identity.voice: Plain and material. We describe the glaze and the making, not the marketing. Example line the brand would write: 'Oatmeal breaks pale over the rim and pools brown in the throwing rings. Thrown and glazed in Brattleboro.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The printer laid out the trade book page three seasons ago and it is the only reference we have; nobody here can open or drive that file. The maker's stamp exists only impressed into the base of the pots, with no drawing of it anywhere, so a single photograph of a bowl foot is the only source for the footer mark.
brand_identity.values: The glaze is the product and must read true on the page, and the book stays airy with one piece to a page and space around it.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Aldervale Mutual - Personalized autumn renewal mailer
client_brief:
Personalised renewal postcards, including eleven correctly separated producer files

For Aldervale Mutual's autumn renewal drop, each household must receive its own address, offer band and assigned producer's photograph. The starting point is the printer's PDF and our spreadsheet.

Please prepare
- Personalised autumn renewal mailer: 61 named exports. The addressee is correct. The offer wording matches the approved copy. The response instructions are readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Cover from people who know your town
brand_identity.sector: A regional mutual carrier writing home and farm cover, sold face to face through local producers across rural Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: central Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Aldervale Mutual Assurance is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is central Vermont, and this commission covers phase 2: personalised renewal mailer.
brand_identity.audience: Homeowners and farm owners aged forty to seventy in small Vermont towns, many insured here for decades, who value a known producer and a fair renewal over the lowest online quote.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year. Mid market and relationship led, not a discount carrier and not a private wealth boutique. Communications stay restrained: one photograph, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer named larger than the offer.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet serif system as set in the 2019 style guide: a text serif for policy copy and addresses, paired with a slightly heavier serif for producer names and headings. Editorial rather than promotional, generous leading, no condensed or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct and adult. We write to the household, never at the market, and we never oversell. Example line the brand would write: "Your renewal is due in October, and your producer, will be glad to walk it through with you."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original design files are gone: the designer retired and took her drive, so the last renewal card survives only as the printer's press PDF. The mark exists cleanly only where it was printed on a producer's business card. One 2019 style guide page (house green, warm grey, the two type families, clear space, and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph) is all the written guidance that remains.
brand_identity.values: Continuity and knowing the policyholder. Households should feel written to by a carrier that still knows them, and the mark is never placed over a photograph.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Lanternwood Folk Fest - Festival programme and wayfinding
client_brief:
Festival programme production from fourteen artist submissions and two old pages

Lanternwood's programme needs one finished page per act, not fourteen different submission styles. We have the lineup sheet, fourteen artist photographs and two old printed programme pages to work from.

Final handoff

 Festival programme: 1 named export. The running order matches the approved lineup. Stage changes are easy to follow. Performer names are readable at print size.

 Festival wayfinding sign: 3 named exports. The destination matches the site information. The direction is unambiguous.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Two days of roots on the farm
brand_identity.sector: A ticketed two day roots and Americana music festival, staged on a working farm and run by a volunteer committee.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: outside Burlington, Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Lanternwood Folk Fest is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is outside Burlington, Vermont, and this commission covers phase 2: keepsake programme and venue wayfinding.
brand_identity.audience: A roots and Americana crowd broadly thirty to sixty, many of them returning regulars who keep the programme, willing to pay for something that feels made rather than mass produced.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Sixty five pounds a day. A considered keepsake register: photographs given real room, editorial type with a proper hierarchy, generous margins, one act to a page breathing rather than a dense fair handout, and never a near empty boutique arts brochure.
brand_identity.typography: A keepsake editorial pairing: a warm serif for act names and headings with a clean, legible sans or serif for set times, stage and biographies. Readable at a glance in a field, generous in a programme, with a clear hierarchy so a reader finds the next act quickly.
brand_identity.voice: Friendly, plain and a little handmade, the voice of a committee that runs the thing itself. Example line the brand would write: "Grab a pint, find your stage, and we will see you down the front."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No working files survive. The previous designer moved to Canada, leaving only two printed programme pages held by the printer (last year's and the year before) plus last year's printed cover. The crest has never existed as a file: it lives only as paint on the canvas banner over the main gate, photographed for reference. Fonts and colours must be inferred from the printed pages.
brand_identity.values: The programme is the keepsake, and the crest is how regulars recognise the festival. Both should feel handmade but properly made, worthy of the wall they end up on.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

2. Part bin label: 18 named exports. The part identifier is readable at rack distance. The label does not substitute a similar part.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A B2B distributor of OEM elevator and electrical replacement components, sold to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Cleveland, Ohio; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Girdermark Components is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Cleveland, Ohio, and this commission covers phase 2: data-sheet and bin-label library.
brand_identity.audience: Working buyers aged thirty five to sixty who have specified this class of part for twenty years and judge a supplier by whether the picture and the numbers match.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Parts from 400 to 9,000 dollars. A flat, even, technical register: one neutral photographic ground, the whole part in frame, generous spec setting, prices plain in the run of the page. Never bright consumer tool styling and never dark cinematic hero work. The bin label answers to a picker at arm's length, so it is bigger, blunter and carries less.
brand_identity.typography: A technical, legible system: a neutral grotesque sans for part numbers, spec tables and labels where clarity at small size and at arm's length is everything, with a plain companion for running copy. No decorative or humanist warmth. Note that no chosen face can reach the printer's sheet or the label house's label, which keep their existing typography.
brand_identity.voice: Blunt, factual and useful. No marketing adjectives, no styling in the words. Example line the brand would write: "Sixteen active parts this season. Specs, codes and prices are exactly as our system holds them."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The division owns none of its own artwork. The spec sheet and the bin label exist only as the flat press PDFs the printer and the label house return. The house mark was lost in an office move and survives only in the printed sheet header and cast into an aluminium nameplate riveted to an old traction machine in the back, photographed for reference. Part photography was shot in house on the bench over several months and does not match.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy above all: the picture and the spec must agree, values are never reworded to fit, and anything that will not fit is raised before it prints.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: SEVE Botanicals - Cosmetic launch label system
client_brief:
Nineteen cosmetic labels with exact ingredient copy and per-shade imagery

SEVE Botanicals needs a launch-label run across two price tiers. We have one physical sample photographed on a phone, nineteen drawdown images and a printer's flat PDF. The imagery needs careful preparation; the compliance copy is not open for creative rewriting.

What we need back
- Cosmetic launch label: 20 named exports. The ingredient wording matches approved copy. The required warning fits at actual label size. The net contents value is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An independent clean beauty house running a prestige apothecary skincare line at counter and a mass everyday colour line on peg.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A small independent clean beauty house in Portland, Oregon, launching nineteen SKUs across two lines this autumn.
brand_identity.about: SEVE Botanicals makes clean, plant led beauty under one house across two very different shelves. Seve Atelier is the apothecary line, sold over a counter, where restraint and an honest ingredient line are the proof of quality. Seve Everyday is the drugstore line on a peg, where a shade has to win in four seconds. Same mark, same values, two registers.
brand_identity.audience: Two buyers under one house: a thirty to fifty five year old counter customer paying for restraint and reading the ingredient list as proof, and a sixteen to thirty five year old drugstore shopper scanning a peg for a shade at arm's length.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Two load bearing tiers. Seve Atelier runs 48 to 85 dollars: quiet, generous negative space, one considered accent, the mark small and confident, the swatch a single honest chip. Seve Everyday runs 6 to 14 dollars: claim forward and shade forward, the shade name and swatch winning at arm's length, the mark holding while small and busy. The same treatment cannot serve both.
brand_identity.typography: A modern editorial pairing that holds across an 85 dollar counter serum and a 6 dollar peg tint without either tier borrowing the other's register: a refined high contrast or clean serif for the wordmark and shade names, with a clear humanist sans for ingredient lines, net weight and batch fields where legibility at small size is critical. Note that no chosen face can reach the printed label, which keeps the label printer's typography.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, botanical and precise, never gushing. Compliance copy stays exactly as written. Example line the brand would write: "One house, two shelves, every shade drawn from the real product."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark was drawn years ago by a designer the house has lost touch with and survives only foil blocked on an old carton, with no dark version at all. The only layout owned is last season's serum label as the flat press PDF the label printer returned. Photography is minimal: one physical sample bottle shot on a phone on kitchen marble, plus nineteen shade drawdowns done on card by the window the same afternoon.
brand_identity.values: Honesty on the shelf: the swatch is the real shade, the ingredient line is exactly as compliance wrote it, and each tier must look right at its own price while staying recognisably one house.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Rivermeadow Trust - Year-end donor acknowledgement system
client_brief:
Replace our manual year-end donor letters with a dependable reusable system

Rivermeadow Trust's office manager spent three weeks preparing acknowledgements last year, and two donors were still missed. We need this December's letters and receipts produced correctly, plus templates the office can reuse next year by changing the data.

The commission

 Donor acknowledgement letter: 19 named exports. The salutation matches the donor record. The acknowledged amount is accurate.

 Donation receipt: 19 named exports. The receipt date is accurate. The donor identity is unambiguous.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Land held in common, kept for good
brand_identity.sector: A small accredited land trust that holds conservation easements and stewards preserves in one Connecticut valley, funded by a few hundred local giving households.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1994, based in the Sedgewater valley, Litchfield County, Connecticut. Four staff, roughly nine hundred acres under easement, a few hundred giving households.
brand_identity.about: Rivermeadow protects the meadows, hollows and river bends of one valley by holding easements and caring for a handful of small preserves. Many of our donors granted the land we now steward, so the relationship is personal and long. We exist so the fields stay fields for the people who walk them.
brand_identity.audience: Local giving households aged 45 to 78, land literate, many of them easement grantors who know the fields by name. Gifts run from 25 dollars to 25,000, a broad community base plus a small leadership circle that carries most of the campaign.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A community land trust, not a national charity. Two registers live in one base: a warm community of small and mid gifts, and a leadership circle giving four and five figures. Every dollar should read as spent on the land, not on ourselves.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headings and running text, set generously with wide margins, paired with a restrained humanist sans for labels and figures. Type should feel like a well kept letter, never like a campaign.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grateful and specific, the voice of a neighbour rather than an institution. It names the field, not the fund. Example: We kept forty more acres in hay this year because you asked us to.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo files left with our first designer and are gone. The mark now survives only on the cast bronze donor plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead, of which we hold one photograph. Approved letter copy, giving level names and thresholds, and the statutory receipt wording still exist as plain text.
brand_identity.values: Permanence of the land, and a personal duty of thanks to every household that gives, whatever the size of the gift.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Emberwell Brew House - Live insert and taproom collateral
client_brief:
Two reusable menu templates for fourteen locations, not fourteen manual edits

Our managers have been retyping the same Emberwell insert in a word processor. That led to a customer finding a different flat-white price twenty minutes down the road. We need two controlled templates that take their local details and prices from the data.

Deliverables
1. Current-menu insert: 15 named exports. The availability wording matches the current record. The price is legible.
2. Taproom counter card: 15 named exports. The store details match this record. The offer is understandable at counter distance.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An independent fourteen room brew house and coffee group across New England, with two flagship kitchens and four counter service coffee rooms.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2013, first room in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. Fourteen rooms across New England, two flagship kitchens, four counter service rooms, one shared coffee program.
brand_identity.about: Emberwell runs fourteen rooms under one name and one coffee program, each in a secondary New England town where it is the good room rather than the cheap one. Same room, same welcome, but every store pays its own rent, so the estate is one brand at fourteen prices.
brand_identity.audience: Morning trade aged 30 to 55 that comes in early and lingers for two hours. Guests who read a menu the way they read a good book and treat loud pricing as a sign they are in the wrong kind of room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Upper middle independent. Plates 14 to 26 dollars, drinks 4.50 to 7. Not a chain and never wanting to read like one: type led, generous, prices set quietly at the end of a line. No combos, no starbursts, no value language.
brand_identity.typography: A warm high contrast serif for dish names and headings, generously leaded, paired with a quiet humanist sans for descriptions and prices. Between the rustic chalkboard cliche and the cold Swiss default: elevated, never shouting.
brand_identity.voice: Warm and plainspoken, a room talking rather than a brand selling. Short lines, no adjectives stacked for effect. Example: The stout is on until the barrel is done, then it is not.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our old logo file is gone. The cleanest surviving version of the mark is the enamel pin on the apron, of which we hold a close photograph. Approved dish names, descriptions, the drinks list, seasonal line names and the fixed allergen statement all survive as plain text, alongside the public store roster.
brand_identity.values: One consistent welcome across the estate, and honest local pricing that a guest never has to question from one town to the next.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Cellar and Cru - Autumn shelf-talker campaign
client_brief:
Autumn shelf talkers that match the bottles and the sellable wine list

Cellar & Cru's autumn selection goes onto the shelf as a collection. We have sixteen photographs covering fourteen wines, taken on two evenings, and an old printer's PDF for the shelf talker.

Please prepare
- Wine shelf talker: 15 named exports. The bottle image matches the named wine. The vintage is accurate. The origin is readable. The price is easy to locate.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street
brand_identity.sector: An independent fine wine merchant selling across the counter to retail customers and to restaurant buyers building by the glass lists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009, on a side street off the main shopping run in Edinburgh, Scotland. A small counter operation, one or two on the floor, an owner who buys the list himself.
brand_identity.about: Cellar & Cru is a merchant, not a shop that happens to sell wine. The owner tastes and chooses every line, and the selection changes with the season. When there is one of us on the floor and eleven people in, the shelf card is how a wine sells itself, so the card carries the grower, the region, the vintage, our note, the score and the price.
brand_identity.audience: Confident domestic drinkers and restaurant buyers aged 40 to 65 who read a shelf card the way a reader reads a review, and who treat visual noise as a signal about the wine behind it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent fine wine. Bottles from 14 pounds to 220. The card is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the line. Never the supermarket aisle, never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet oldstyle serif for wine names and running notes, set with air, paired with a plain grotesque for regions, vintages and figures. Readable at 40 to 65, restrained rather than loud or fashionable.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, measured and honest, the owner describing a wine as if standing beside you. It says what a wine is and is not, without hyperbole. Example: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original mark artwork went with the designer who moved abroad. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the letterpressed compliments card he had made for us, carrying the mark at about 45mm. The autumn list, buyer's notes, scores and prices arrive from the till export.
brand_identity.values: A selection chosen by one buyer with a point of view, and a shop floor that sells wine honestly even when nobody is free to talk.

values.Wine: Clos des Galets Muscadet Sevre et Maine sur Lie
values.Buyer Note: Loire white, sur lie, bone dry and saline with a lees-y roundness. The house everyday white and a natural with oysters or a Friday takeaway.
Dry Alsace riesling, taut and citrus-driven with a stony finish. Not sweet. Good with charcuterie, roast pork or a ripe washed-rind cheese.
Classic Loire sauvignon: cut grass, gooseberry and wet flint, high and bright acidity. The safe, smart glass of white for almost any table.
Unoaked chardonnay from Kimmeridgian marl, lean and oyster-shell mineral. Chill it well and drink it with anything from the sea.
Pale dry Provence rose, red berry and citrus pith over a saline finish. Aperitif rose for the last of the warm evenings.
Coastal Italian white, green almond, lemon and a faintly bitter herbal edge that loves salt and olive oil. Easy, savoury, under the radar.
Featherweight Mosel kabinett with a touch of sweetness held up by racing acidity. Low in alcohol, high in charm, brilliant with spice.
Austrian gruner, white pepper and green apple with a crisp savoury bite. The wine for tricky vegetables and anything from the garden.

The co-op red, and the wine I put in more hands than any other on the shelf. Carignan and grenache off old bush vines, unoaked, bottled young and honest. Bramble, black pepper and a little garrigue, soft enough to drink on a Tuesday but with real grip underneath. Fourteen pounds, and it drinks well above that so long as you open it a good hour before dinner.

values.Wine: Domaine des Escaliers Cote Brune Syrah
values.Buyer Note: A single-vineyard northern Rhone syrah off the steep brown schist above the river, co-fermented with a little viognier the way the hill has always done it. Black olive, cracked pepper, cured meat and violets, over a tannin still coiled tight. This wants five years in the cellar, or a decanter and a long lunch if you cannot wait that long.

A mature Piedmontese nebbiolo from a great vintage, ten years on and only now unwinding. Tar, dried rose, sour cherry and a dusting of woodsmoke over that famous grip of tannin and acid. Do not chill it and do not rush it: open it an hour ahead, pour it beside something with fat and salt, and let the middle of the bottle show you why we bought the allocation.
Light-framed village Burgundy, red cherry and forest floor over silky tannin. Serve it cool. The gateway to proper Pinot.
Southern Rhone grenache and syrah, warm and generous: kirsch, thyme and cocoa with a peppery lift. A fireside red at a fair price.

The wine that changes how people think about Beaujolais. Cru gamay off granite, whole-bunch and unfiltered, so there is a savoury reduction on first pour that blows off into black cherry, iron and crushed violets. Serve it with a light chill against charcuterie or a roast chicken. If you still think gamay is thin and sweet, this is the bottle I would hand you to argue with.

task_name: Vanguard Motors - Forecourt sales card system
client_brief:
Forecourt cards for current stock, with honest paint and highlight handling

Vanguard Motors has fourteen cars on the forecourt, but the feed still includes vehicles sold or reserved. Please reconcile the stock before producing the A4 window cards. The photography also needs care: some panels were overexposed during the shoot.

Final handoff

 Forecourt sales card: 15 named exports. The pictured vehicle matches this stock number. The finance wording follows the approved text. The vehicle specification is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: An independent prestige used vehicle dealership selling to retail buyers and part exchange customers from a single forecourt.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2006, one forecourt in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. A small independent holding about fourteen cars at a time, buying selectively rather than to volume.
brand_identity.about: Vanguard holds around fourteen carefully bought cars at a time and sells to people who have already decided roughly what they want and are choosing where to buy it. The card in the windscreen is the first thing a buyer meets, before anyone walks out, so it has to answer their two questions honestly: what is this car, and what does it cost.
brand_identity.audience: Private retail buyers aged 35 to 60 who have narrowed the choice online, driven a distance to see one specific car, and are deciding whether this dealer is careful.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent prestige used. Cars from 18,000 pounds to 95,000. Photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short spec of what differs between examples, the price plainly set and the finance line legible but secondary. Never the budget lot register, never a manufacturer brochure with no price.
brand_identity.typography: A confident low contrast serif or sturdy grotesque for the marque and headline, paired with a clean neutral sans for the spec block, price and finance footer. Careful and quiet, neither discount loud nor brochure sparse.
brand_identity.voice: Factual, unhurried and confident, a dealer who lets the car and the spec do the talking. No exclamation, no urgency. Example: One owner, full history, the colour it says on the card and the colour it is on the forecourt.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The shield artwork is long gone. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door, weathered by several winters, carrying the shield at about 180mm. The current stock, specs and prices arrive from the stock feed, and the finance wording is fixed by the broker.
brand_identity.values: Cars bought with care and sold without spin, and a forecourt where the card and the vehicle always agree.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Continental Cup - Squad press and partner kit
client_brief:
Expand our licensed player-card production to the full stocked squad

The licensing partner has taken the full Continental Cup squad. We now need the eighteen-player material reconciled against the stock roster and produced from last season's printer PDF.

Scope
1. Squad player press sheet: 21 named exports. The portrait belongs to the named player. The squad facts match the register.
2. Player partner graphic: 20 named exports. The player number is clear. The competition identity is visible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The whole squad, under the lights.
brand_identity.sector: Officially licensed collectible trading cards for a touring North American and European club football tournament, sold into grocery, newsstand and hobby channels through a national licensing partner.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: touring competition, Western Europe and North America; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Continental Cup 2026 is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is touring competition, Western Europe and North America, and this commission covers phase 2: squad press run and partner files.
brand_identity.audience: Collectors aged sixteen to forty five who buy officially licensed sets beside other marquee cards, in grocery aisles, at newsstands and in hobby shops. They notice when a card in the pack looks like it came from somewhere else.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A flagship licensed pack retailing around fourteen dollars, positioned above community and league sets and below fine-art prints. It must read as a marquee cup collectible, saturated and cinematic, never as a cheap programme or a gallery piece.
brand_identity.typography: A heavy, near-metallic display face for the player name and squad number, set large and confident, paired with a clean condensed sans for the position, club line and set year. The type should feel like a stadium scoreboard, not a school sports day.
brand_identity.voice: Bold, terse, terrace-proud. Copy is short and declarative. Example line the brand would write: 'Eighteen players. One set. Every card earns its place in the sleeve.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no surviving design file or logo artwork. The tournament mark now exists only on printed things: the sole reference is a handheld photograph of a pitch-side sponsor board carrying the mark in one deep ink on a pale board. It has to be recovered as usable artwork before it can be placed at any size.
brand_identity.values: A licensed set is a promise: every player is who the card says, and the look holds across the whole squad rather than favouring a hero. Consistency in the sleeve is the product.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

task_name: Ferncroft Nursery - Spring plant tag system
client_brief:
Spring plant tags with four complete, non-overlapping department files

Ferncroft Nursery needs the spring tag run rebuilt from last year's printed artwork and the growers' spreadsheet. There are eighteen varieties in the source material, but only stocked varieties should reach the final run.

What we need back
- Plant variety tag: 22 named exports. The photograph depicts the named variety. The care instruction matches the authoritative register. The tag remains readable at rack size.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Grown for the people who ask where it came from.
brand_identity.sector: Retail horticulture: an heirloom specialty nursery and garden centre selling perennials, herbs, shrubs and a short specimen list from its own benches across four planting departments.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A small heirloom grower in Litchfield County, Connecticut, selling from its own benches, with a growing office and four department benches each tended by a different person.
brand_identity.about: Ferncroft Nursery grows heirloom and specialty stock for gardeners who read the botanical name first. Everything is sold off the bench with a tag that reads like a plant person wrote it. Spring opening is the last Saturday of April, and every plant on the rack needs its tag by then.
brand_identity.audience: Gardeners aged thirty five to sixty five who buy for provenance, read the Latin name, and ask where the stock was grown. They distrust a rack where one tag looks like a different shop.
brand_identity.price_positioning: An heirloom specialty grower at eighteen to ninety five dollars a plant, above the six dollar big-box rack and below a fine-press botanical print. The tag is provenance-led and botanical-forward: the Latin carries, the price sits small, the photograph is a supporting note.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif with real presence for the common and botanical names, the Latin set in italic beneath, paired with a quiet, small sans for the care line, pot size and price. Restraint is the point: the price should never shout.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, knowledgeable, unhurried, the voice of a grower. Example line the brand would write: 'Slow to establish, then generous for decades. Give it morning sun and patience.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no design files. The two tags the printer ran last spring survive only as press PDFs, and the nursery mark exists only routed and painted into the slate sign at the gate, captured in one handheld photograph. The mark and the printed care icons have to be recovered before they can go anywhere new.
brand_identity.values: Provenance and honesty on the bench: the name on the tag is the right name, and the whole rack reads as one careful hand. Restraint signals quality here.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Marrow and Vane - Exhibition wall-label system
client_brief:
Exhibition wall labels and artwork records, with installer files by room

Marrow & Vane is hanging forty-one works. We need the spring printer's label artwork reused, not redesigned, and a reconciled photographic record from the interns' two shoots.

The commission

 Exhibition wall label: 42 named exports. The work identity matches this accession record. The artist attribution is accurate. The curatorial text is readable at installation distance.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Arts and culture: a mid-career commercial gallery mounting selling exhibitions of contemporary work for collectors and institutional curators.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A commercial gallery in Philadelphia hanging across three rooms, run by a director with a small registrar and installation team.
brand_identity.about: Marrow and Vane is a Philadelphia gallery that mounts selling shows for collectors and curators. The house look is austere and generously spaced: the label and the checklist stay quiet so the work carries the room. Their autumn exhibition hangs forty one works by nine artists across three rooms.
brand_identity.audience: Collectors and institutional curators, plus a press list. Readers who scan a medium line for provenance and expect the gallery to signal seriousness through restraint rather than through decoration.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Works from six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars. At this level the label is small, quiet type high on a large card with unprinted stock beneath, no rules, no colour, no logo on the card. It must read as a selling show, not a community group show and not a museum survey.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained institutional system: a quiet text face at a small size for the title, artist, medium, dimensions and accession, with the botanical restraint of a gallery hand. No display drama; the measure and the white space do the work. The checklist and the labels read as one house.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, precise, factual. The gallery states rather than sells. Example line the brand would write: 'Nine artists. Three rooms. Eighteen September through the second of November.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no layout file for the labels; only the printer's spring press PDF survives as the look to keep. The gallery mark exists as an etched brass plate beside the door and a single photograph of it, and has to be recovered as real artwork before it can sit on the checklist.
brand_identity.values: Restraint as respect for the work: the label serves the art and the record is accurate to the last accession number. The institution shows its seriousness by staying quiet.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

task_name: Ember and Oak - Restaurant launch reel system
client_brief:
We are opening the second room at Ember and Oak and need a launch package that makes people hungry before they read a word. The food should lead: real char, visible texture and a room that feels alive. Please build a deliberate short edit from the service footage, then make the upright and square versions feel composed in their own right. The booking message needs a proper ending, not a logo dropped over the last available frame. We also need the cover, window poster and dish cards to look like the same launch. This campaign is deliberately silent.

Deliverables
1. Restaurant launch reel: 1 named export. The opening makes the food recognisable. The final card identifies Ember and Oak. The booking action is readable.
2. Restaurant vertical reel: 1 named export. The food stays legible through reframing. The final booking action stays within the safe area.
3. Restaurant square reel: 1 named export. The restaurant identity is visible. The edit has a deliberate beginning and ending.
4. Restaurant reel cover: 1 named export. The restaurant name is readable.
5. Restaurant launch poster: 1 named export. The booking action is readable. The char retains visible texture.
6. Dish callout card: 3 named exports. The callout matches the pictured dish.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. Speech-led work requires supplied or explicitly authorised synthetic speech; do not invent documentary speech.
- Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live-action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: What fire does to good meat.
brand_identity.sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
brand_identity.about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
brand_identity.audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.
brand_identity.typography: A bold, warm display face for dish names and the end card, set large and immediate, paired with a sturdy sans for the one-line description and price. The type has to carry over fire behind it: confident, appetite-first, never a restrained editorial serif.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
brand_identity.values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
